习近平的新斯大林主义议程雄心勃勃，风险巨大，而且在他登上权力巅峰之初，前景似乎并不乐观。作为胡锦涛的接班人，习近平之所以被选中，很可能是因为他被视为一位软弱的领导人，缺乏广泛的强大盟友网络。与江泽民和胡锦涛领导的根深蒂固的派系对抗可能十分危险，因为在他们执政的二十年间，他们已将自己的支持者安插在党内要职。采取更严厉的镇压手段并恢复国家主导的经济政策，很可能会遭到来自基层的抵制。事实上，在习近平于2012年底正式就任中共中央总书记之前，人们一直在争论他是否是一位隐藏的改革者，其议程比他的前任们更加自由化。直到2013年2月，他关于苏联解体的（男性）言论被泄露后，一些人才开始感到不祥之兆。 2013年4月，一份由中央办公厅发布的关键文件——即所谓的“九号文件”——的泄露内容引发广泛关注（稍后详述），这加剧了人们对习近平将党带向更强硬和反西方方向的担忧。到2013年夏天，习近平对社交媒体发起大规模打压，显然他的新斯大林主义计划已经全面展开。





War on Corruption





反腐败战争


Prior to Xi's rise, the party had frequently launched anticorruption campaigns to discipline its officials. These campaigns were relatively short in duration, targeting mostly mid- to lower-level functionaries to reestablish party authority and to appease public anger. Although these campaigns seemed to curb corruption for a brief period of time as officials tended to lay low to avoid being caught, their long-term impact was modest at best.12 Politically, the top leaders were careful not to weaponize corruption investigations against their rivals. The two exceptions—the fall of Politburo members Chen Xitong (in 1995) and Chen Liangyu (in 2006) on corruption charges—proved the rule.

在习近平上台之前，中共曾多次发起反腐运动以惩戒官员。这些运动持续时间相对较短，主要针对中低层官员，旨在重塑党的权威并平息公众的愤怒。尽管这些运动似乎在短期内遏制了腐败，因为官员们往往会低调行事以避免被抓，但其长期影响充其量也只能说是微乎其微。在政治上，最高领导人谨慎地避免将反腐调查武器化，以打击政敌。仅有的两个例外——政治局委员陈希同（1995年）和陈良宇（2006年）因腐败指控而下台——恰恰证明了这一原则。

The apparent infrequent weaponization of corruption in elite rivalry was most likely the result of the fragile balance of elite power in the post-Mao era, which prevented the top leader—Deng, Jiang, or Hu—from resorting to this tool, except on rare occasions (Deng did not touch it at all). According to the CCP charter, only the Politburo has the power to expel a member of the Central Committee for violation of party discipline.13 This meant that a top leader had to win support from rival factions to topple any senior official on corruption charges. The presence of rival factions on the Politburo raised this procedural hurdle as all members shared a similar interest in preventing one faction from dominance through the subterfuge of anticorruption investigations.

精英阶层权力斗争中腐败手段的运用似乎并不频繁，这很可能是后毛泽东时代精英权力平衡脆弱的结果。这种脆弱的平衡使得最高领导人——邓小平、江泽民或胡锦涛——除了极少数情况外，很少会动用这一手段（邓小平更是从未使用过）。根据中共党章，只有政治局才有权因违反党纪而开除中央委员。这意味着，最高领导人必须赢得其他派系的支持，才能以腐败指控罢免任何高级官员。政治局内部存在不同派系，这增加了程序上的难度，因为所有委员都希望通过反腐调查来阻止某个派系独揽大权。

In practice, the party's procedural stipulations grant enormous investigative authority to the head of the Central Discipline Inspection Commission (CDIC), the sole body empowered to investigate senior officials.14 Instructively, to prevent the party chief from using anticorruption investigations to purge his rivals, top leaders in the post-Mao era usually picked for this position someone who was not a close ally of the top leader. Chen Yun, the first chief of the CDIC, was actually Deng's rival. During the Jiang period, the head of the CDIC was someone from a rival faction. In Hu's first term, the CDIC was led by an apparatchik perceived to be close to Jiang. In his second term, another official who had quickly risen under Jiang was in charge of the CDIC. Even though the Politburo or the PSC must approve the opening of a formal investigation into a senior official, the head of the CDIC could play a critical role in this process. As the CDIC would conduct "preliminary verification" of alleged violations, it was in a position to gather sufficient evidence to make it difficult for the Politburo to block an investigation.

实际上，党的程序规定赋予中央纪委主任极大的调查权，而中央纪委是唯一有权调查高级官员的机构。值得注意的是，为了防止党的总书记利用反腐调查清除异己，后毛泽东时代的领导人通常会选择与最高领导人关系不密切的人担任这一职务。首任中央纪委主任陈云实际上是邓小平的竞争对手。江泽民时期，中央纪委主任则来自敌对派系。胡锦涛第一任期内，中央纪委主任是一位被认为与江泽民关系密切的官员。胡锦涛第二任期内，另一位在江泽民手下迅速晋升的官员掌管了中央纪委。尽管对高级官员展开正式调查必须得到政治局或国家政协的批准，但中央纪委主任在这一过程中可以发挥关键作用。由于 CDIC 将对涉嫌违规行为进行“初步核实”，因此它能够收集到足够的证据，使政治局难以阻止调查。

The practice of appointing someone who was not an ally of the party chief to be the head of the CDIC ended in November 2012 when Xi's close associate, Wang Qishan, was chosen to take it over. Xi likely had insisted on giving Wang the anticorruption portfolio so that he would have a trusted ally to supervise his war on corruption. With his direct control of the CDIC's investigative capabilities, Wang could be counted on to produce dossiers containing incriminating evidence against rivals that was too strong for the Politburo members to reject.

任命非党魁盟友担任中央反腐败局局长的惯例在2012年11月终结，当时习近平的亲信王岐山被任命为局长。习近平很可能坚持让王岐山担任反腐败职务，以便拥有一个值得信赖的盟友来监督他的反腐斗争。凭借王岐山对中央反腐败局调查能力的直接掌控，他能够提供足以令政治局委员无法驳回的、包含对手确凿证据的档案。

In terms of objectives, targets, ferocity, and duration, Xi's anticorruption campaign differed qualitatively from all previous such efforts. What defines Xi's war on corruption is its objective of systematically dismantling the networks of power formed under Jiang and Hu, neutralizing rivals, and establishing his dominance.15 Also notable is the fact that Xi's campaign focused on high-level officials and their allies in local governments, whereas previous campaigns had ensnared mostly mid-level or junior officials. Tactically, Xi opted for much harsher penalties. Disgraced top leaders, including a former PSC member (Zhou Yongkang), four former Politburo members (Bo Xilai, Guo Boxiong, Xu Caihou, and Sun Zhengcai), and Hu Jintao's former chief of staff (Ling Jihua) were given life sentences. In terms of duration, previous anticorruption drives were short-lived, but Xi's campaign was open-ended. In 2022, for example, a decade after the beginning of his campaign, the party claimed to have investigated (in reality, detained) 32 "centrally supervised" (zhongguan) high-ranking officials, the most since 2018, and 410 mid-level officials.16 Because 2022 was the year of the scheduled Twentieth Party Congress at which Xi planned to secure an unprecedented third term, it seemed likely that he dialed up the anticorruption campaign to deter potential opposition. Xi escalated the purge further in 2023 and 2024, likely to shore up his authority during a period when the Chinese economy was struggling with deflation and an epic real estate crash. In 2023, 47 "centrally supervised" officials were investigated; in 2024, 60 such officials, including two retired provincial party chiefs, were investigated.17 Anticorruption investigations thus became Xi's potent weapon to intimidate and purge rivals and potential threats.

从目标、力度、持续时间来看，习近平的反腐运动与以往所有反腐行动都截然不同。习近平反腐战争的本质在于系统性地瓦解江泽民和胡锦涛时期建立的权力网络，清除异己，巩固自身统治地位。值得注意的是，习近平的反腐运动重点打击地方政府的高级官员及其盟友，而以往的反腐运动主要针对中层或基层官员。在策略上，习近平采取了更为严厉的惩罚措施。包括前国家政协委员周永康、前政治局委员薄熙来、郭伯雄、徐才厚和孙正才以及胡锦涛的前幕僚长凌继华在内的多位落马的高层领导人被判处无期徒刑。就持续时间而言，以往的反腐运动往往昙花一现，而习近平的反腐运动则没有明确的结束日期。例如，在习近平发起反腐运动十年后的2022年，中共声称调查（实际上是拘留）了32名“中央监管”高级官员，这是自2018年以来人数最多的一次，此外还有410名中层官员被调查。由于2022年是中共二十大召开之年，习近平计划在会上确保史无前例的第三个任期，因此他加大反腐力度以震慑潜在的反对派似乎很有可能。习近平在2023年和2024年进一步升级了清洗行动，这很可能是为了在中国经济遭受通货紧缩和房地产市场崩盘的双重打击之际巩固自己的权威。2023年，共有47名“中央监管”官员受到调查； 2024年，包括两名退休省委书记在内的60名此类官员接受了调查。反腐调查由此成为习近平恐吓和清除对手及潜在威胁的有力武器。

A review of the course of Xi's anticorruption drive shows that, from the outset, he had clear political priorities. The first was to neutralize any threat to his power posed by those with ties to the domestic security apparatus and the military. Consequently, the first prominent target of Xi's purge was Zhou Yongkang, a former PSC member and a powerful domestic security chief with close ties to Jiang. An investigation into Zhou began almost as soon as Xi rose to the top. To build a case against Zhou, the CDIC detained several senior officials who had worked with him and could provide incriminating materials. The CDIC also cast a wider net, investigating family members and relatives of the main targets because they could be forced to cooperate. In the case against Zhou Yongkang, it took roughly one year for the CDIC to complete its investigations. The PSC formally placed him under investigation in July 2014; eleven months later, he was convicted of accepting bribes totaling 130 million yuan and leaking state secrets to his personal fortune teller, for which he received a life sentence.18

回顾习近平的反腐历程，可以看出，从一开始，他的政治优先事项就十分明确。首要目标是消除任何与国内安全机构和军队有联系的人对其权力构成的威胁。因此，习近平清洗行动的首要目标是周永康，他曾是国家安全委员会委员，也是与江泽民关系密切的国内安全部门高官。习近平上台后不久，对周永康的调查便立即展开。为了搜集证据，国家安全监察局拘留了几名曾与周永康共事、可能提供不利证据的高级官员。国家安全监察局还扩大了调查范围，对主要目标人物的家人和亲属进行调查，因为他们可能被迫配合。在对周永康的调查中，国家安全监察局耗时约一年才完成。国家安全监察局于2014年7月正式对周永康展开调查。 11个月后，他因收受贿赂1.3亿元人民币和向私人算命先生泄露国家机密而被判处无期徒刑。

The fall of Zhou, the first former PSC member to be jailed in the post-Mao era, sent shockwaves throughout the party-state as it showed that no one was safe under Xi's rule. But that was just the beginning. In March 2014, shortly after the PSC approved an investigation into Zhou's activities, Xu Caihou, a former Politburo member and vice chairman of the CMC, was placed under investigation as well. Several months later, Xu was expelled from the party and transferred to a military court for prosecution. He died in March 2015, before his trial. Xu's colleague and fellow Jiang ally, former Politburo member and CMC vice chairman Guo Boxiong, was investigated for corruption in April 2015 and received a life sentence in July of the following year.

周恩来是毛泽东时代后首位被监禁的前公安委员，他的落马震惊了整个党国体制，表明在习近平的统治下，没有人是安全的。但这仅仅是开始。2014年3月，在公安委员会批准对周恩来的活动进行调查后不久，前政治局委员、中央军委副主席徐才厚也被列入调查名单。几个月后，徐才厚被开除党籍，并被移送军事法庭审判。他在2015年3月去世，当时他尚未受审。徐才厚的同事、江泽民的盟友、前政治局委员、中央军委副主席郭伯雄于2015年4月因腐败问题接受调查，并于次年7月被判处无期徒刑。

The purge of Xu and Guo served another one of Xi's critical objectives—to seize control of the military. Aware that his own survival would be imperiled without the support of the PLA, Xi launched the most far-ranging purge of the senior ranks of the military since the 1971 fall of Lin Biao, a legendary general and Mao's main ally during the Cultural Revolution. By November 2015, Xi's campaign had ensnared forty-five generals for alleged corruption.19 The purge of generals suspected of being disloyal became a constant feature of Xi's rule. In subsequent years, more high-ranking generals, including a former chief of the General Staff and head of the PLA's Political Department, fell victim to Xi's anticorruption investigations. According to a tally by the highly respected journal Caixin, seventy-five generals were arrested between November 2012 and October 2019.20 The removal of generals who had been promoted when Guo and Xu were effectively in charge of military personnel matters (2002-2012) accomplished two goals for Xi: With one stroke, he neutralized the potential threat posed by their supporters in the military and paved the way to appoint his own supporters to those positions.

徐和郭的清洗服务于习近平的另一个关键目标——掌控军队。习近平深知，若失去解放军的支持，他的统治将岌岌可危，因此发动了自1971年林彪倒台以来规模最大的军队高层清洗。林彪是毛泽东在文化大革命期间的主要盟友，也是一位传奇将领。到2015年11月，习近平的这场运动已将45名将军卷入腐败指控。清洗被怀疑不忠的将军成为习近平统治时期的一项常态。在随后的几年里，包括一名前总参谋长和解放军政治部部长在内的更多高级将领成为习近平反腐调查的受害者。据权威媒体财新统计，2012年11月至2019年10月期间，共有75名将军被捕。20 清除那些在郭文贵和徐正昌实际掌管军人事务期间（2002-2012年）晋升的将军，对习近平而言实现了两个目标：一举消除了他们在军队中的支持者构成的潜在威胁，并为任命自己的支持者担任这些职位铺平了道路。

Xi deployed the same tactic to purge senior officials and their supporters in local governments. As shown by the number of officials ranked at bureau level or above who were criminally prosecuted during Xi's first term, his campaign evidently was focusing on senior and mid-level officials in order to destroy entire networks.21 Because the party did not disclose the ranks of those officials who had been criminally prosecuted during the Hu era, we have to use data from the Jiang era as a comparison. According to the CDIC, between October 1992 and June 1997, 1,673 bureau-level and 78 ministerial- or provincial-level officials were prosecuted for corruption. Between October 1997 and September 2002, Jiang's last term in office, 2,422 bureau-level and 98 ministerial- or provincial-level officials were prosecuted for corruption. During Xi's first term, by comparison, 8,900 bureau-level and 440 ministerial- or provincial-level officials were prosecuted for corruption, representing a huge increase in each category.22

习近平运用同样的策略清洗地方政府的高级官员及其支持者。从习近平第一任期内被刑事起诉的局级及以上官员人数可以看出，他的运动显然聚焦于中高级官员，旨在摧毁整个腐败网络。由于党没有公布胡锦涛时期被刑事起诉官员的级别，我们只能使用江泽民时期的数据进行比较。根据中国国家反腐败委员会的数据，1992年10月至1997年6月，共有1673名局级官员和78名部级或省级官员因腐败被起诉。1997年10月至2002年9月，即江泽民的最后一个任期内，共有2422名局级官员和98名部级或省级官员因腐败被起诉。相比之下，习近平第一任期内，因腐败被起诉的局级官员有8900人，部级或省级官员有440人，两类官员被起诉的人数均大幅增加。

A close examination of the highest-ranking targets of Xi's anticorruption campaign reveals that he prioritized the purge of full and alternate members of the Central Committee who typically occupied the most important provincial and ministerial positions. Again, the contrast with his predecessors is illuminating. Between 1992 and 2012, only seventeen full and alternate members of the Central Committee were prosecuted for corruption. During Xi's first decade in power, forty-nine full and alternate members of the Central Committee were punished for corruption (and most sentenced to long prison terms).23

仔细审视习近平反腐运动中最高级别的打击目标，可以发现他优先清洗的是中央委员和候补委员，这些人通常担任着最重要的省级和部级职务。与他的前任相比，这一对比同样发人深省。1992年至2012年间，仅有17名中央委员和候补委员因腐败受到起诉。而在习近平执政的第一个十年里，有49名中央委员和候补委员因腐败受到惩罚（其中大多数人被判处长期监禁）。

In his second term, Xi's top priority was to purge the domestic security apparatus of officials who were suspected of political disloyalty. As a complementary effort, the purge of the so-called political-legal sector would completely cement Xi's control of the coercive apparatus. In January 2018, two months after Xi got a second term, he launched a campaign ostensibly to root out organized crime and its "protective umbrellas"—officials in the domestic security apparatus suspected of shielding criminals from the law.24 The campaign quickly claimed several high-ranking officials, including secretaries of CCP provincial political-legal committees (who typically had served as provincial police chiefs) and an incumbent vice minister of public security, Sun Lijun, who was allegedly the ringleader of a cabal of corrupt officials in the security apparatus.25

习近平第二个任期内的首要任务是清洗国内安全机构中涉嫌政治不忠的官员。作为一项配套措施，对所谓政法部门的清洗将彻底巩固习近平对强制机构的控制。2018年1月，习近平连任两个月后，他发起了一场表面上旨在铲除有组织犯罪及其“保护伞”——即国内安全机构中涉嫌包庇犯罪分子的官员——的运动。这场运动迅速导致多名高级官员落马，其中包括中共省级政法委书记（他们通常曾担任省级公安局局长）以及时任公安部副部长孙立军，据称他是安全机构中一个腐败官员集团的头目。

In February 2021 Xi launched a separate campaign, "Education and Rectification of the Nation's Political-Legal Ranks," explicitly targeting officials in the domestic security sector. As this purge was overseen by Xi's loyal ally Chen Yixin and launched roughly twenty months before the Twentieth Party Congress, at which Xi was expected to seek a third term, its political objectives—removing security officials suspected of disloyalty and intimidating potential threats—were self-evident. A large number of officials fell victim to this round of purges, and many had held senior positions. Fu Zhenghua, a former Central Committee member and executive vice minister of public security, was given a suspended death sentence in September 2022. Another former vice minister of public security who had overseen anticorruption in the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China's secret police, was detained in March 2022 and given a suspended death sentence in January 2023. By July 2022 this campaign had brought down nearly three dozen senior local law enforcement officials, including nine secretaries and deputy secretaries of the provincial legal-political committees.26 Many lower-ranking law enforcement officials also fell into the dragnet. Within the first six months of the campaign, 12,576 police officers had turned themselves in.27 Following this purge, Xi was able to install his loyalist, Wang Xiaohong, as the new minister of public security. Chen Yixin became minister of the MSS in March 2023, thus giving Xi total control over the security apparatus.

2021年2月，习近平发起了一场名为“国家政法干部教育整顿”的运动，目标直指国内安全部门官员。这场清洗运动由习近平的忠实盟友陈宜鑫负责，且在中共二十大召开前约二十个月启动（习近平预计将在二十大上寻求第三个任期），其政治目的——清除被怀疑不忠的安全官员并恐吓潜在威胁——显而易见。大量官员在这场清洗中落马，其中许多人身居要职。前中央委员、公安部常务副部长傅正华于2022年9月被判处死刑，缓期执行。另一位曾任公安部副部长、负责国家安全部反腐工作的官员于2022年3月被捕，并于2023年1月被判处死刑，缓期执行。截至2022年7月，这场运动已导致近30名地方高级执法官员落马，其中包括9名省级政协书记和副书记。许多低级执法官员也未能幸免。在运动开展的头六个月内，就有12576名警察自首。这场清洗之后，习近平得以安插自己的亲信王晓红担任新的公安部长。陈宜新于2023年3月出任国家安全部部长，从而使习近平对安全机构拥有了绝对的控制权。

Despite the scale of the purges, Xi introduced institutional changes to make anticorruption investigations an even more powerful instrument against potential threats. Three weeks after his installation as party chief, the Politburo issued a set of rules limiting official entertainment, meetings, issuance of documents, use of government vehicles, and media coverage of the activities of party leaders.28 Violators would be punished (although these rules apparently do not apply to Xi, who has received lavish media coverage).

尽管清洗规模巨大，习近平仍推行了一系列制度改革，使反腐调查成为应对潜在威胁的更强有力的工具。在他就任中共中央总书记三周后，政治局颁布了一系列规定，限制官方招待、会议、文件签发、公务车辆使用以及媒体对党领导人活动的报道。违规者将受到惩罚（尽管这些规定显然不适用于习近平，他获得了大量的媒体曝光）。

In addition, Xi revised the party's disciplinary code and the procedures for anticorruption investigations to bolster his personal authority and to make any expression of dissent against the top party leadership a punishable infraction of the law. A comparison of the party's disciplinary code formalized under Hu in December 2003 and its revised version published in October 2015 reveals several crucial changes made to suppress potential opposition to Xi's authority. Most notably, the revision added several punishable political violations, such as "wantonly discussing major policies of the party-state and undermining the party's centralized unity, smearing the images of the party and the state, denigrating the top leadership of the party and the state, or distorting the history of the party or of the military." Unauthorized public statements on major policy issues that should be within the "purview of the party center" could result in severe penalties as well.29

此外，习近平还修订了党的纪律守则和反腐败调查程序，以巩固其个人权威，并将任何反对党最高领导层的异议言论都定为违法行为。对比胡锦涛于2003年12月正式制定的党的纪律守则和2015年10月发布的修订版，可以发现其中几项关键改动旨在压制对习近平权威的潜在反对。最显著的是，修订版增加了几项政治违规行为，例如“肆意讨论党国重大政策，破坏党的集中统一，抹黑党和国家的形象，诋毁党和国家的最高领导层，歪曲党和军队的历史”。未经授权就属于“党中央职权范围”的重大政策问题发表公开声明，也可能受到严厉处罚。

To expand the party's disciplinary reach beyond party members, Xi set up a super agency—the National Supervisory Commission—in March 2018. Even though this commission was to be staffed by the same personnel as the CDIC, the law establishing it gave it power to investigate and punish nonparty members who work in SOEs and in publicly funded entities, such as hospitals, universities, cultural institutions, and nongovernmental organizations. The commission and its local agencies were also empowered to detain the subjects of investigation for up to six months without court approval or judicial review.30

为了将党的纪律管辖范围扩大到党员之外，习近平于2018年3月成立了一个超级机构——国家监察委员会。尽管该委员会的人员组成与中央监察委员会相同，但设立该委员会的法律赋予了它调查和惩处在国有企业和公共资助实体（如医院、大学、文化机构和非政府组织）工作的非党员的权力。该委员会及其地方机构还被授权在未经法院批准或司法审查的情况下，拘留被调查对象长达六个月。

It is tempting to credit Xi's unrelenting crackdown for curbing official corruption. But the continuous stream of disgraced officials accused of corruption years after the beginning of Xi's campaign suggests that his war on corruption had at most a partial impact on curbing corruption. In all likelihood, Xi's other policies—such as suppressing press freedoms and civil society and shifting resources to the state sector—either facilitated or made it difficult to fight corruption.31 This outcome should not be surprising because the principal objective of Xi's crackdown on corruption was for him to gain political dominance. In this regard, the campaign has evidently served him well.

人们很容易将习近平不遗余力的反腐行动归功于遏制官员腐败。然而，在习近平反腐运动开始数年后，仍有源源不断的官员因腐败指控而身败名裂，这表明他的反腐战争至多只起到了部分作用。很可能，习近平的其他政策——例如压制新闻自由和公民社会、将资源转移到国有部门——要么助长了腐败，要么使反腐工作更加困难。这一结果并不令人意外，因为习近平反腐的主要目的是为了巩固其政治统治地位。从这个角度来看，这场运动显然对他大有裨益。





Power Grab





权力争夺


Taking advantage of the momentum of his anticorruption drive, Xi wasted little time to consolidate power. He scored his greatest victory in October 2016 when the Central Committee formally granted him the title of "core leader." (Jiang's designation, conferred on him by Deng, was a less significant achievement.)32 Underscoring Xi's newly obtained political supremacy, the Central Committee communique announcing the elevation of his status called on the party to "firmly and unswervingly preserve and defend the authority of the party center and its centralized and unified leadership," an obvious reference to Xi.33

凭借反腐运动的势头，习近平迅速巩固了权力。2016年10月，中央正式授予他“核心领导人”的称号，这是他取得的最大胜利。（姜孝林的称号由邓小平授予，意义相对较小。）为了凸显习近平新近获得的政治至高地位，中央在宣布提升其地位的公报中呼吁全党“坚定不移地维护和捍卫党的中央权威和集中统一领导”，这显然是指习近平。

Besides gaining this coveted title, Xi had scored other major victories. He successfully grabbed power that normally would belong to the premier. This was accomplished by establishing "leading small groups" that effectively took away power to make policy on specific issues from the State Council. For instance, he formed the "Central Leading Small Group on Comprehensive Deepening Reform" in November 2013 and appointed himself as its chairman. Because of its broad mandate, any new reform or policy change required its approval, thus allowing Xi to control more directly the overall political and economic agendas. Other new leading small groups Xi established and also headed at the beginning of his first term oversaw cybersecurity and military reform. In addition, he chaired preexisting leading small groups on foreign policy, Taiwan affairs, and finance.34

除了获得这一令人垂涎的头衔外，习近平还取得了其他重大胜利。他成功攫取了通常属于总理的权力。这是通过建立“领导小组”实现的，这些小组有效地从国务院手中夺取了在特定问题上制定政策的权力。例如，他在2013年11月成立了“中央全面深化改革领导小组”，并任命自己为组长。由于该小组拥有广泛的职权范围，任何新的改革或政策变化都需要其批准，从而使习近平能够更直接地控制整体政治和经济议程。习近平在其第一任期之初还成立并领导了其他一些新的领导小组，负责网络安全和军事改革。此外，他还担任了此前已有的外交政策、台湾事务和金融等领导小组的组长。

Another tactic he used to amass power was a systematic revision of the party's organizational rules and the updating of its resolutions on history to formalize and legitimize his personal authority and expand his power. Immediately after the conclusion of the Nineteenth Party Congress in October 2017, the Politburo issued the "Regulations on Strengthening and Maintaining the Party Center's Centralized and Unified Leadership." Although the full text of this document has not been made public, the official media have disclosed some of its key points. First, the regulations emphasize absolute loyalty to Xi, as indicated by the statement that the Politburo must "resolutely maintain General Secretary Xi Jinping's status as the core of the party center and the entire party." In addition, the regulations require Politburo members to "proactively report major issues to the party center for deliberation, studiously implement decisions and plans of the party center, and make timely reports on their significant progress ... (and) self-consciously struggle against words and acts that ... harm the party center's centralized leadership and unity." To enforce these rather abstract requirements, the regulations include an unprecedented rule mandating that Politburo members must submit annual written self-evaluations of their job performance to the general secretary (i.e., Xi). This provision, which recalls the Maoist "self-criticisms" the late dictator regularly forced his colleagues to make, grants Xi additional leverage over Politburo members, who must perform this annual exercise in full awareness of the adverse consequences of an unfavorable evaluation of their performance. In addition to the Politburo members, other senior leaders, such as the members of the Secretariat of the Central Committee, the CDIC, the party organizations within the Standing Committee of the NPC, the State Council, the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, are required to submit similar self-evaluations to the PSC and the Politburo, thus allowing Xi to more directly control the critical central organs of the regime.35

他巩固权力的另一策略是系统性地修改党的组织规则和历史决议，以正式化和合法化其个人权威并扩大权力。2017年10月中共十九大闭幕后，政治局立即印发了《关于加强和维护党中央集中统一领导的规定》。虽然该文件的全文尚未公开，但官方媒体已披露了其部分要点。首先，该规定强调对习近平的绝对忠诚，其中指出政治局必须“坚决维护习近平总书记作为党中央和全党核心的地位”。此外，该规定要求政治局委员“主动向党中央报告重大问题供其审议，认真执行党中央的决定和计划，及时报告取得的重大进展……（并）自觉反对损害党中央集中领导和团结的言行”。为了落实这些较为抽象的要求，相关规定中包含一项前所未有的条款，强制政治局委员每年向总书记（即习近平）提交书面工作绩效自评报告。这项规定让人想起毛泽东时代强迫其同僚进行“自我批评”的做法，赋予习近平对政治局委员更大的影响力，因为政治局委员必须在充分意识到不利评价后果的情况下完成这项年度自评。除了政治局委员之外，其他高级领导人，例如中央书记处书记、中央情报局书记、全国人大常委会各级党组织、国务院、全国政协、最高人民法院和最高人民检察院的官员，也被要求向政协和政治局提交类似的自评报告，从而使习近平能够更直接地控制政权的关键中央机关。

To bolster the legitimacy of his personal authority, Xi undertook to rewrite a landmark document issued under Deng to prevent the return of a Mao-like figure. In February 1980 the Central Committee had approved a historic document, the "Guiding Principles for Inner-Party Political Life" that explicitly established collective leadership and prohibited personality cults.36 As this document would stand in the way of Xi's goal of replacing collective leadership with one-man rule and fortifying his power with a personality cult, the Central Committee, most likely under pressure from Xi, revised it at the same plenum that granted Xi the title of "core leader" in October 2016. A comparison of the two documents shows that the revision completely removes the prohibition against personality cults and downplays the principle of collective leadership, while, in an obvious reference to Xi, placing strong emphasis on the authority of the "core leadership."37

为了巩固个人权威的合法性，习近平着手修改邓小平时期颁布的一份具有里程碑意义的文件，以防止出现类似毛泽东的人物。1980年2月，中央委员会批准了一份历史性文件——《党内政治生活指导原则》，该原则明确确立了集体领导制，并禁止个人崇拜。由于这份文件会阻碍习近平以一人统治取代集体领导制、并通过个人崇拜巩固自身权力的目标，中央委员会很可能是在习近平的压力下，于2016年10月的同一次全会上对其进行了修订，并在会上授予习近平“核心领导人”的称号。对比两份文件可知，修订后的文件完全删除了禁止个人崇拜的条款，淡化了集体领导制的原则，同时，显然是针对习近平，着重强调了“核心领导人”的权威。

The party's celebration of its centennial in 2021 provided another opportunity for Xi to burnish his credentials as a great leader. The Central Committee issued a historic resolution in November of that year, ostensibly to summarize the party's experiences during the past century. But in a comparison of two similar documents, the one issued by Mao in 1945 and the other by Deng in 1981, Xi's version focuses mostly on the party's self-proclaimed accomplishments during Xi's nine years in power—the so-called "New Era." Roughly 19,000 of the resolution's 36,200 characters are devoted to Xi's period in power, while the sections covering the prior ninety-one years of party history contain only 10,000 characters.38

2021年，中共庆祝建党百年，这为习近平提供了又一次巩固其伟大领袖形象的机会。同年11月，中央委员会发表了一份历史性决议，表面上是为了总结党在过去一个世纪中的经验。但对比毛泽东1945年和邓小平1981年发表的两份类似文件，习近平的版本主要侧重于党自诩的在其执政九年——即所谓的“新时代”——取得的成就。这份36200字的决议中，约有19000字用于描述习近平的执政时期，而涵盖此前91年党史的部分仅有10000字。

Xi's efforts to revive a personality cult go well beyond passing resolutions glorifying his leadership. Coverage of his activities dominates the official media. His published works are on prominent display in bookstores. Judging by the number of published volumes of his collected works, those by Xi exceed those by all other Chinese leaders, including Mao. In February 2022 the first volume of Selected Letters of Xi Jinping was published, implying that future volumes would be forthcoming (among Xi's predecessors, only one volume of Mao's Selected Letters was published). This honor was not accorded to Deng or any other revolutionary leader. By June 2022, four volumes of Xi's speeches on governance had been published, equaling the number of volumes of Mao's Selected Works released during Mao's time in office (Deng, Jiang, and Hu were limited to three volumes each). In 2023 the party released two additional volumes, Selected Readings of Xi Jinping's Works as well as a college textbook, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics in the New Era.

习近平重塑个人崇拜的努力远不止于通过决议歌颂其领导。官方媒体对其活动的报道占据主导地位。他的著作在书店里占据显眼位置。从其著作集的出版卷数来看，习近平的著作集超过了包括毛泽东在内的所有其他中国领导人。2022年2月，《习近平书选》第一卷出版，这意味着后续卷册也将陆续面世（在习近平的前任领导人中，毛泽东的《毛泽东书选》仅出版了一卷）。邓小平和其他任何革命领袖都没有获得过这样的殊荣。截至2022年6月，习近平的《治国理政》四卷本已出版，与毛泽东在任期间出版的《毛泽东文选》卷数持平（邓小平、江泽民和胡锦涛的《毛泽东文选》均为三卷）。 2023年，党又出版了两卷著作：《习近平著作选读》和一本大学教材：《习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想》。

Judging by the outcome of the Nineteenth Party Congress in October 2017, Xi's neo-Stalinist tactics evidently paid off. On the eve of the gathering, Xi arrested Sun Zhengcai, a Politburo member affiliated with the Jiang faction who had been seen as a potential candidate for the position of party chief. (Sun was later sentenced to life in prison for alleged corruption.) The prosecution of Sun was evidently carried out to intimidate rival factions that might have been standing in the way of Xi's plans to remake the top party leadership at the upcoming party congress.

从2017年10月召开的中共十九大结果来看，习近平的新斯大林主义策略显然奏效了。在十九大召开前夕，习近平逮捕了政治局委员孙正才，此人是江泽民派的成员，曾被视为党总书记的潜在人选。（孙正才后来因涉嫌腐败被判处无期徒刑。）显然，对孙正才的起诉是为了震慑那些可能阻碍习近平在即将召开的党代会上重塑党内最高领导层的反对派。

As expected, the congress cemented Xi's political dominance: Two-thirds of the twenty-five Politburo members were his acolytes. Of the six other members of the PSC, Xi could count at least four as allies (one of them was in charge of the powerful CDIC). His loyalists were also made party chiefs of the most important provinces, such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Chongqing, and Xinjiang.

正如预期的那样，这次大会巩固了习近平的政治统治地位：25名政治局委员中有三分之二是他的亲信。在另外6名政治常委中，至少有4名是习近平的盟友（其中一人掌管着权力强大的中央投资局）。他的亲信还被任命为北京、上海、广东、重庆和新疆等重要省份的党委书记。

Most important, at the same party congress Xi revealed his intention of breaking the implicit two-term limit for the general secretary. At the Seventeenth Party Congress in 2007, when Hu was about to start his second term, the party designated his successor, Xi, after intense internal jockeying. A decade later, however, Xi prevented the designation of an heir-apparent since no newly promoted members of the PSC were under 55 (the ideal age for a potential successor because that person would be 60 when appointed party chief at the next party congress and then could serve two five-year terms).

最重要的是，在同一次党代会上，习近平透露了他打算打破总书记两届任期限制的意图。2007年，在胡锦涛即将开始第二任期的十七大上，经过激烈的内部角逐，党内指定了习近平为他的接班人。然而，十年后，习近平阻止了指定接班人的行动，因为当时没有新晋升的全国政协委员低于55岁（55岁是潜在接班人的理想年龄，因为这个人将在下届党代会上被任命为党的总书记时年满60岁，可以连任两届，每届五年）。

Having stacked the Politburo with supporters, Xi immediately took the required procedural steps to break the implicit term limits. Of his three positions—CCP general secretary, chairman of the CMC, and state president—only one, the state president—was subject to an explicit constitutional limit.

习近平在政治局安插了大量支持者后，立即采取必要程序步骤打破了不成文的任期限制。在他的三个职位——中共中央总书记、中央军委主席和国家主席——中，只有国家主席一职受到宪法的明确限制。

Even though this position is largely ceremonial, the party chief must also hold the title of state president to engage in top-level foreign affairs. Diplomatic protocols usually do not allow foreign heads of state to meet the leader of a political party. Xi thus had to abolish the constitutional term limit for the state president as a first step to extend his rule indefinitely.

尽管这一职位在很大程度上是礼仪性的，但党的总书记也必须兼任国家主席，才能参与最高级别的外交事务。外交礼仪通常不允许外国元首会见政党领袖。因此，习近平不得不废除宪法规定的国家主席任期限制，以此作为无限期延长其统治的第一步。

In January 2018 the Politburo approved a package of constitutional amendments that contained the abolition of the presidential term limit even though the meeting's press release did not refer to this particular amendment. In March the annual NPC meeting, the rubber-stamp parliament, duly approved the abolition of presidential term limits, signaling Xi's intention to serve indefinitely.39

2018年1月，政治局批准了一揽子宪法修正案，其中包括取消国家主席任期限制，尽管会议新闻稿并未提及此项修正案。同年3月，橡皮图章式的全国人大年会正式批准取消国家主席任期限制，表明习近平有意无限期任职。

At the Twentieth Party Congress in October 2022, Xi easily obtained a third term as CCP general secretary, and by the time of the conclusion of the congress, he had achieved total political dominance. Implicit norms on term and age limits no longer applied to him or to his followers. In addition to giving himself a third term, Xi kept on the Politburo two supporters who were over the implicit mandatory retirement age of 68, but he also forced out two rivals, Premier Li Keqiang and PSC member Wang Yang, who were under 68. A former Politburo member, 59-year-old Hu Chunhua, was not reappointed because he was a protégé of Hu Jintao (no relation) and a possible contender for future party chief. At the Twentieth Party Congress, Xi also prevented the designation of a potential successor.

在2022年10月召开的中共二十大上，习近平轻松连任中共中央总书记，并在大会闭幕时实现了绝对的政治掌控。关于任期和年龄限制的隐性规范对他及其追随者不再适用。除了让自己连任第三届外，习近平还保留了两位超过68岁法定退休年龄的支持者在政治局任职，同时排挤了两位未满68岁的竞争对手——国务院总理李克强和国家政协委员汪洋。一位59岁的前政治局委员胡春华没有获得连任，因为他是胡锦涛（与胡锦涛并无亲属关系）的门生，也是未来党总书记的潜在人选。在中共二十大上，习近平还阻止了潜在接班人的指定。





Flash the Sword





闪剑


Shortly after Xi delivered his political manifesto, "Some Questions on Maintaining and Developing Socialism with Chinese Characteristics," at the Central Party School in January 2013, the General Office of the Central Committee, which at that time was directed by Xi's close ally, Li Zhanshu, issued the now-infamous Document No. 9, "Communique on the Current State of the Ideological Sphere." The document identifies "erroneous ideological trends" that must be "watched." The document was issued on April 22, 2013, but it was never made public, most likely because it would reveal Xi's hard-line ideological stance. When it was leaked in August 2013, its contents confirmed Xi's hostility to liberal ideas.

2013年1月，习近平在中央党校发表了题为《关于坚持和发展中国特色社会主义的若干问题》的政治宣言后不久，时任中央办公厅主任、习近平的亲密盟友栗战书发布了臭名昭著的9号文件——《关于当前意识形态领域的状况通报》。该文件指出了一些必须“警惕”的“错误思想潮流”。这份文件于2013年4月22日发布，但从未公开，很可能是因为它会暴露习近平的强硬意识形态立场。2013年8月，该文件被泄露，其内容证实了习近平对自由主义思想的敌视。

According to Document No. 9, the party must tighten control over the media and guard against seven subversive ideas—Western constitutional democracy, universal values, civil society, economic neo-liberalism, the Western concept of press freedom, historical nihilism (exposing the party's dark past), and questioning the nature of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In addition to listing these ideas that could directly undermine party legitimacy, Document No. 9 also sounds an alarm about subversive dissident activities, such as agitation for political reform, human rights, press freedom, and public disclosure of officials' assets. It warns that Western diplomatic missions, media, and NGOs were engaging in various activities inside of China to cultivate opposition forces and to conduct "cyber infiltration." According to the authors of Document No. 9, the West represents an existential threat because it seeks regime change through "Westernizing, splitting, and color revolutions."40 Despite the dire warnings in Document No. 9, the party waited until August 2013 before launching a full-scale crackdown on the dangerous trends identified in the document.

根据第九号文件，党必须加强对媒体的控制，防范七种颠覆性思想——西方宪政民主、普世价值、公民社会、经济新自由主义、西方新闻自由观念、历史虚无主义（揭露党的黑暗历史）以及质疑中国特色社会主义的本质。除了列举这些可能直接损害党的合法性的思想外，第九号文件还对颠覆性异议活动发出警告，例如鼓动政治改革、人权、新闻自由以及公开官员财产等。文件警告称，西方外交机构、媒体和非政府组织正在中国境内开展各种活动，以培养反对派力量并进行“网络渗透”。根据《第九号文件》的作者所述，西方构成生存威胁，因为它试图通过“西化、分裂和颜色革命”来实现政权更迭。尽管《第九号文件》发出了严峻的警告，但党直到2013年8月才对文件中指出的危险趋势展开全面镇压。

Liangjian, or flash your sword, is an apt metaphor for Xi's get-tough-on-dissent approach, and, unsurprisingly, it quickly became a popular phrase in the official media despite its association with intimidation and violence. In all likelihood, Xi first invoked this phrase at the National Meeting on Publicity and Theoretical Work in August 2013, even though the phrase cannot be found in the published version of his speech. Nevertheless, two clues suggest Xi himself likely used this phrase at this conference. First, the published official version of Xi's speech, most probably sanitized, urges the party to "maintain an initiative and fight successful offensive battles" (zhudong zhang) on fundamental political issues.41 Second, the official media published summaries of the reflections by all thirty-one provincial propaganda chiefs (who almost certainly attended the conference) on Xi's speech. Notably, ten used the phrase "dare to flash your sword" (ganyu liangjian). As it is customary for provincial propaganda chiefs to regurgitate key points made by the party chief (in this case, Xi), it is reasonable to conclude that they were merely parroting one of the most emphatic points Xi made at the conference.42

“亮剑”一词恰如其分地比喻了习近平对异议采取的强硬态度，尽管它与恐吓和暴力联系在一起，却迅速成为官方媒体的常用语，这并不令人意外。习近平很可能在2013年8月的全国宣传和理论工作会议上首次使用了这一短语，尽管在其讲话的正式版本中并未出现。然而，有两条线索表明习近平本人很可能在这次会议上使用了这一短语。首先，习近平讲话的正式版本（很可能经过了删改）敦促党在根本政治问题上“保持主动，打赢进攻战”。其次，官方媒体刊登了31位省级宣传部长（他们几乎肯定参加了会议）对习近平讲话的总结。值得注意的是，其中10位部长使用了“敢于亮剑”这一短语。由于地方宣传负责人通常会复述党总书记（在本例中是习近平）的要点，因此可以合理地推断，他们只不过是在鹦鹉学舌地重复习近平在会议上强调的要点之一。

Events that transpired subsequently show what liangjian meant—it was a concerted preemptive campaign against a potential "color revolution," marking a fundamental shift from the party's stance toward dissent in the post-Tiananmen era. Both Jiang and Hu had adopted a defensive or reactive strategy of repression: They usually cracked down on dissent in response to overt challenges to party authority or actions by the country's small community of dissidents who crossed the regime's threshold of tolerance. From the very beginning, however, Xi's campaign assumed a preemptive or offensive nature. Instead of responding to overly aggressive challenges to one-party rule, his campaign targeted the very sources that could generate, maintain, and reproduce such threats: social media, human rights activists, lawyers, liberal academics, ethnic minorities, NGOs and their foreign supporters, and protest movements in Hong Kong. This campaign is also notable for its blitzkrieg tactics: The crackdown was carried out at lightning speed. Targets of the repression received harsh punishments, extra-judicial mass incarcerations, or long prison sentences, which the party had eschewed during the pre-Xi period. In another qualitative departure from his predecessors' tactics in dealing with threats to the party, Xi sought to reinforce his metaphoric "sword" through institutionalization and the party-controlled legal system. As a result, new bureaucracies overseeing cybersecurity and national security were established. New laws and regulations, such as those governing foreign NGOs, cybersecurity, and internet use, were issued to add a veneer of legality to the emerging neo-Stalinist order.

随后发生的事件表明了“两建”的含义——这是一场针对潜在“颜色革命”的有预谋的先发制人运动，标志着中共在后天安门时代对待异议的立场发生了根本性转变。江泽民和胡锦涛都采取了防御性或被动的镇压策略：他们通常只在异议人士公开挑战党的权威，或少数异议人士越过政权容忍底线时才会进行镇压。然而，习近平的这场运动从一开始就呈现出先发制人、主动出击的性质。他没有被动应对对一党专政过于激进的挑战，而是将目标对准了那些可能产生、维持和复制此类威胁的源头：社交媒体、人权活动人士、律师、自由派学者、少数民族、非政府组织及其外国支持者，以及香港的抗议运动。这场运动的另一个显著特点是其闪电战式的策略：镇压行动以闪电般的速度展开。镇压对象遭受了严厉的惩罚、法外大规模监禁或长期监禁，而这些在习近平之前是中共所避免的。与前任应对党内威胁的策略相比，习近平在另一项质的转变中，试图通过制度化和党控的法律体系来强化其象征性的“利剑”。因此，负责网络安全和国家安全的新官僚机构得以建立。新的法律法规，例如关于外国非政府组织、网络安全和互联网使用的法律法规，相继出台，为正在形成的“新斯大林主义”秩序披上了一层合法性的外衣。

The first target of this preemptive campaign was social media, which had gained unprecedented reach and influence due to the popularization of smart phones. Not coincidentally, the crackdown on social media began on August 20, 2013, the same day that the national publicity conference ended. Police in Beijing arrested Qin Zhihui, a well-known blogger with a mass following, on charges of fabricating online rumors. Three of his colleagues were arrested as well. Charles Xue, a Chinese American businessman with over twelve million verified followers on Weibo (a Chinese microblogging website), was detained on August 23 for "patronizing a prostitute." He later appeared on national TV confessing his crime, evidently against his own will. Several hundred netizens were arrested, detained, or punished between August 20 and 31 in this nationwide crackdown, which was carried out to implement Xi's order for a "serious blow" against internet "rumors."43 On September 6 the party-controlled Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate issued a joint "legal interpretation" that made "internet libel" a criminal offense. If a piece of "libelous information" receives more than five thousand clicks or is forwarded more than five hundred times, its author will receive severe punishment.44 The effect of "flashing" this metaphorical "sword" was instant: by singling out well-known social media influencers, the party tamed China's once-vibrant social media practically overnight, a feat few had thought was either conceivable or feasible.45

这场先发制人的行动首要目标是社交媒体，智能手机的普及使其获得了前所未有的影响力和覆盖面。并非巧合的是，对社交媒体的打压始于2013年8月20日，也就是全国宣传大会闭幕的同一天。北京警方以捏造网络谣言的罪名逮捕了拥有大量粉丝的知名博主秦志辉，他的三名同事也一同被捕。8月23日，拥有超过1200万微博认证粉丝的美籍华裔商人薛志辉因“嫖娼”被拘留。之后，他出现在国家电视台，被迫承认了自己的罪行。 8月20日至31日，在全国范围内开展的这场打击网络谣言的行动中，数百名网民被逮捕、拘留或处罚。此次行动旨在落实习近平关于“重击”网络“谣言”的命令。9月6日，最高人民法院和最高人民检察院联合发布法律解释，将“网络诽谤”定为刑事犯罪。如果一条“诽谤信息”的点击量超过5000次或转发量超过500次，其作者将受到严厉处罚。这一举措的效果立竿见影：通过重点打击知名的社交媒体影响者，中共几乎在一夜之间驯服了中国曾经充满活力的社交媒体，这在当时几乎是不可想象的。

To institutionalize the party's strict control over cyberspace, Xi established the "Central Leading Small Group on Cybersecurity and Informatization" in February 2014. He personally chaired this committee and appointed a party propaganda official, Lu Wei, to direct its daily operations. (In March 2018 Xi elevated the "leading group" to the status of a central commission and made himself its chairman.) Lu Wei, a ruthless apparatchik, faithfully implemented Xi's orders and instituted a series of new censorship measures (including a requirement that all social media users register their accounts with their real names so the authorities could identify them).46 The Cyber Security Law passed in November 2016 is another attempt to solidify party control of the internet as it strictly forbids anyone from "using the internet to engage in activities that endanger state security, reputation, and interests, or instigate the subversion of state power, the socialist system . . . fabricate and disseminate false information."47

为了将党对网络空间的严格控制制度化，习近平于2014年2月成立了“中央网络安全和信息化领导小组”。他亲自担任该小组组长，并任命党的宣传官员卢伟负责指导其日常运作。 （2018年3月，习近平将“领导小组”提升为中央委员会，并亲自担任主席。）冷酷无情的官僚陆伟忠实地执行了习近平的命令，并推行了一系列新的审查措施（包括要求所有社交媒体用户使用真实姓名注册账户，以便当局识别用户身份）。2016年11月通过的《网络安全法》是进一步巩固党对互联网控制的又一举措，该法严格禁止任何人“利用互联网从事危害国家安全、声誉和利益的活动，或者煽动颠覆国家政权、社会主义制度的活动……捏造、散布虚假信息”。

Around the same time as the crackdown on social media, the party began a separate campaign against well-known human rights activists and dissidents. During the Jiang and Hu periods, the regime had dealt with most dissidents using less repressive tactics. They were placed under routine surveillance and occasionally harassed, but most remained free. However, under Xi's new policy of "flashing your sword," they were not only arrested but sentenced to long prison terms under trumped-up charges, such as "picking quarrels and provoking trouble" and "disturbing public order"—the two criminal charges the regime favored using against its opponents. In July 2013 Xu Zhiyong, a Beijing-based legal scholar who had gained fame a decade earlier for petitioning the NPC to abolish the harsh antivagrancy regulation, was arrested for "disturbing public order." Xu had founded the New Citizens Movement in 2010 to promote constitutional rule, equal rights, and government transparency. During the Hu period, the authorities largely left him alone, even allowing him to run for—and win two times—a seat in a district people's congress in Beijing. Apparently to make Xu an example, the party sentenced him to four years in prison in 2014. (In 2020 he was rearrested and later received a sentence of fourteen years.)

在打压社交媒体的同时，中共也开始对知名人权活动人士和异见人士发起另一场运动。在江泽民和胡锦涛执政时期，政权对待大多数异见人士的手段相对温和。他们受到例行监视，偶尔也会受到骚扰，但大多数人仍然享有自由。然而，在习近平“亮剑”的新政策下，他们不仅遭到逮捕，还被以捏造的罪名判处长期监禁，例如“寻衅滋事”和“扰乱公共秩序”——这两项罪名正是政权惯用的对付反对派的手段。2013年7月，常驻北京的法学学者徐志勇因“扰乱公共秩序”被捕。十年前，他曾因向全国人大请愿废除严苛的反流浪条例而声名鹊起。徐志勇于2010年创立了“新公民运动”，旨在倡导宪政、平等权利和政府透明。胡锦涛执政时期，当局基本上没有干涉徐勇，甚至允许他两次竞选并当选北京市区人大代表。显然是为了杀鸡儆猴，中共于2014年判处徐勇四年有期徒刑。（2020年他再次被捕，后被判处十四年有期徒刑。）

The party flashed its biggest metaphoric sword on July 9, 2015, when it conducted a nationwide crackdown on human rights lawyers. Police detained more than three hundred lawyers who had been active in the rights defense movement. Many were later debarred and imprisoned. Like the campaign to silence social media in August 2013, the blitzkrieg against human rights lawyers instantly destroyed a nascent but largely informal political movement seeking modest incremental change through the legal system that the party itself had established and controlled. Based on the limited success of these lawyers in seeking judicial relief for their clients during the less repressive Hu era, they did not present a serious threat to one-party rule. But in Xi's "new era," no form or degree of dissent could be tolerated. Indeed, in the eyes of Xi's regime, human rights lawyers exploiting the loopholes and formal procedures of China's legal system were far more dangerous because they were more resourceful, sophisticated, and difficult to deal with than the less well-educated workers and farmers. They could not only expose the regime's hypocrisy and brutality but also set examples for challenging its rule peacefully and, on occasion, successfully.48

2015年7月9日，中共挥舞着其最具象征意义的利剑，在全国范围内对人权律师展开镇压。警方拘留了三百多名积极参与维权运动的律师，其中许多人随后被吊销律师执照并遭到监禁。如同2013年8月的社交媒体封杀行动一样，这场针对人权律师的闪电战瞬间摧毁了一场萌芽但主要以非正式形式存在的政治运动。这场运动旨在通过中共自身建立和控制的法律体系，寻求渐进式的、温和的变革。在胡锦涛执政时期，这些律师为客户寻求司法救济的成效有限，因此并未对一党专政构成严重威胁。但在习近平的“新时代”，任何形式、任何程度的异议都无法容忍。事实上，在习近平政权眼中，那些利用中国法律体系漏洞和形式程序的维权律师远比那些受教育程度较低的工人和农民更加危险，因为他们更加足智多谋、老练世故，也更难对付。他们不仅可以揭露政权的虚伪和残暴，还可以为和平挑战其统治树立榜样，而且有时还能取得成功。

Labor organizers came under attack in April 2014 when a court in Guangzhou convicted eleven labor activists for "disturbing public order." In December 2015 at least three leaders of the workers' rights movement in Guangzhou were arrested for "gathering a crowd to disturb social order."49 Supporters of labor rights were not left alone, either. In the fall of 2018, police conducted a nationwide crackdown on self-proclaimed Marxist students involved in protesting against violations of labor rights.50 Compared with the repressive tactics previously used by the party against labor organizers, which mainly consisted of intimidation and harassment, Xi's campaign against labor rights activists was decidedly an escalation in terms of state-sponsored violence as it used criminal charges, such as "picking quarrels and provoking trouble," to convict and imprison them.51 The crackdown on other civil society organizations similarly followed this new approach of "authoritarian legality."52

2014年4月，广州一家法院以“扰乱公共秩序”的罪名判处11名劳工维权人士有罪，劳工组织者因此遭受攻击。2015年12月，广州至少三名工人权益运动领导人因“聚众扰乱社会秩序”被捕。劳工权益的支持者也未能幸免。 2018年秋季，警方在全国范围内对自称马克思主义者的学生进行镇压，这些学生参与了抗议劳动权利受到侵犯的活动。50 与此前党对劳工组织者主要采取的恐吓和骚扰等镇压手段相比，习近平对劳工权利活动人士的镇压行动在国家暴力方面无疑有所升级，因为它使用了“寻衅滋事”等刑事指控来定罪和监禁他们。51 对其他公民社会组织的镇压也同样遵循了这种新的“威权法治”方式。52

Liberal academics were not spared in the crackdown. Academics whose lectures or online speech contained views contradicting or violating official orthodoxy were either warned or dismissed. Based on a partial record of academics fired under Xi's rule, this campaign started in late 2013 when a law professor at the prestigious East China University of Political Science and Law in Shanghai was fired for posting an online article critical of the party.53 Although the precise number of academics fired thereafter is unknown, as of the end of 2019, dozens of university faculty had reportedly lost their jobs because of their political views.54 A small number of professors received even more severe punishment. A prominent law professor at Tsinghua University who had published an open letter critical of Xi and the party's handling of the Covid-19 pandemic in early 2020 was arrested on a trumped-up charge of "patronizing a prostitute" in July 2020 and subsequently fired.55 In Guizhou, an academic was sentenced to four and half years in prison in August 2023 for his outspoken views.56

自由派学者也未能幸免于这场镇压。那些在讲座或网络言论中表达与官方正统观点相悖或违宪的学者，要么遭到警告，要么被解雇。根据习近平执政期间部分被解雇学者的记录，这场运动始于2013年末，当时上海著名学府华东政法大学的一位法学教授因发表批评党的网文而被解雇。尽管此后被解雇的学者确切人数尚不清楚，但截至2019年底，据报道已有数十名大学教师因其政治观点而失去工作。少数教授甚至受到了更严厉的惩罚。清华大学一位知名法学教授在2020年初发表公开信，批评习近平和中共对新冠疫情的处理方式，同年7月被以捏造的“嫖娼”罪名逮捕，随后被解雇。在贵州，一位学者因其直言不讳的观点于2023年8月被判处四年半有期徒刑。

To ensure the routinization of ideological control on university campuses, the party increased its use of student informants and installed video cameras in classrooms to record professors' lectures. Again, even though the authorities began to deploy student informants after the crushing of the student-led prodemocracy movement in 1989, the use of student informants under Xi is far more systematic, extensive, and aggressive.57 Another measure of institutionalizing ideological repression on university campuses is the issuance of the "Ten Professional Principles" by the Ministry of Education in November 2018. Principle no. 3 explicitly prohibits faculty from "using classrooms, forums, lectures, information networks, and other channels to express and share erroneous views or to fabricate false or unhealthy information."58 Obviously, this "principle" gives the authorities a handy tool to punish academics for their political views.

为了确保意识形态控制在大学校园的常态化，中共加大了对学生线人的利用，并在教室安装摄像头录制教授的讲课。尽管当局在1989年镇压学生民主运动后就开始部署学生线人，但习近平领导下的学生线人使用更加系统化、广泛化和激进。教育部于2018年11月发布的《十项职业原则》是大学校园意识形态压制制度化的另一项举措。原则三明确禁止教师“利用课堂、论坛、讲座、信息网络等渠道表达和传播错误观点，或者捏造虚假、有害信息”。显然，这条“原则”为当局提供了一个便捷的工具，可以惩罚持有政治观点的学者。

Despite official restrictions, Western NGOs were able to establish a modest presence inside China prior to Xi's rise. After Xi became party chief, however, the regime's paranoia about foreign NGOs, perceived to be potential instigators of "color revolutions," reached a new level. In April 2016 the NPC passed a new law on foreign NGOs that imposed onerous administrative burdens and significantly raised security risks for operating in China. Among other things, the law orders foreign NGOs to register with Chinese police, the designated enforcement agency that has broad authority over nearly all aspects of the operations of foreign NGOs. For example, the requirement that foreign NGOs must provide the police with advance notice of their planned activities is obviously intended to discourage their activities.59 The law, which affected more than seven thousand foreign NGOs when it went into effect, allowed no grace period, forcing many to suspend operations immediately. By early 2018, only 350 foreign NGOs had reregistered under the new law, suggesting that 95 percent of the foreign NGOs might have exited the country.60 Judging by this metric, the law has evidently achieved its objective.

尽管受到官方限制，西方非政府组织在习近平上台前仍能在中国建立起一定规模的影响力。然而，习近平担任中共中央总书记后，当局对外国非政府组织的担忧——认为它们可能煽动“颜色革命”——达到了新的高度。2016年4月，全国人大通过了一项关于外国非政府组织的新法律，该法律对在华开展活动的外国非政府组织施加了繁重的行政负担，并显著提高了其安全风险。该法律规定，外国非政府组织必须在公安机关登记注册，而公安机关是指定的执法机构，对外国非政府组织的几乎所有活动都拥有广泛的管辖权。例如，要求外国非政府组织必须提前向警方通报其活动计划，显然是为了阻止它们的活动。该法律生效时影响了七千多个外国非政府组织，且未给予任何宽限期，迫使许多组织立即停止运营。截至 2018 年初，仅有 350 家外国非政府组织根据新法律重新注册，这表明 95% 的外国非政府组织可能已经离开该国。60 从这一指标来看，该法律显然已经达到了其目标。

As surveillance of the population constitutes a key pillar of Xi's neo-Stalinist order, the party has made the upgrading of mass surveillance a top state priority. In the post-Tiananmen era, the regime had rolled out two high-tech surveillance programs, Golden Shield and Skynet, that allowed police to utilize a vast digital database, a cyber surveillance apparatus, and networked cameras and sensors to keep track of the activities and speeches of Chinese people. After Xi came to power, the surveillance state received several technological and organizational upgrades. The first program singled out for upgrading was grid management, which divides a community into several grids, each with roughly a thousand residents. The grid is supervised by an official and patrolled by a grid attendant, each equipped with a mobile device to report any incidents. This program was listed as a key task at the Central Committee plenum in November 2013.61 In June 2014 the State Council issued an outline to build a "social credit" system.62 Although this technologically challenging system remains a work in progress, its potential surveillance capabilities can make the dystopia depicted in George Orwell's 1984 a reality in China. In May 2015 the government launched a new high-tech surveillance project, Sharp Eyes, which uses newer technologies, such as facial recognition and cloud computing, to upgrade Skynet and extend video surveillance to the countryside.63

由于对民众的监控是习近平新斯大林主义秩序的关键支柱，中共已将升级大规模监控列为国家首要任务。在天安门事件后，中共推出了两项高科技监控计划——“金盾”和“天网”，使警方能够利用庞大的数字数据库、网络监控设备以及联网摄像头和传感器来追踪中国民众的活动和言论。习近平上台后，监控体系在技术和组织方面进行了多项升级。首当其冲的升级项目是网格化管理，它将一个社区划分为若干个网格，每个网格大约有1000名居民。每个网格由一名官员监管，并由一名网格管理员巡逻，他们都配备了移动设备，用于报告任何事件。该项目在2013年11月中央全会上被列为重点任务。2014年6月，国务院发布了构建“社会信用体系”纲要。尽管这一技术难度极高的体系仍在完善中，但其潜在的监控能力可能使乔治·奥威尔《1984》中描绘的反乌托邦景象在中国成为现实。2015年5月，政府启动了一项名为“锐眼”的高科技监控项目，该项目利用人脸识别和云计算等新技术升级“天网”，并将视频监控扩展到农村地区。





Crackdown on the Periphery





打击外围势力


The party has always perceived China's peripheral regions, whether areas with large populations of ethnic minorities such as Tibet and Xinjiang or newly regained territories such as Hong Kong and Macau, as areas harboring separatists or dissidents who are supported by hostile external forces. In the post-Tiananmen era the party abandoned a more conciliatory approach in favor of a more repressive policy to maintain China's grip on these areas. However, as resistance to Chinese rule continued in spite of the tightened security measures, the party under Xi decided to escalate the repression to an unprecedented level.

中共一直将中国周边地区，无论是西藏、新疆等少数民族聚居区，还是香港、澳门等新近收复的领土，都视为滋生分裂分子或异见人士的温床，并认为他们受到外部敌对势力的支持。天安门事件后，中共放弃了较为温和的政策，转而采取更为强硬的手段来维护对这些地区的控制。然而，尽管安保措施不断加强，反抗中国统治的呼声依然不减，习近平领导下的中共决定将镇压升级到前所未有的程度。

Xinjiang, the northwestern province that was not formally incorporated into China until the late nineteenth century, quickly became the epicenter of conflict between its largest ethnic minority group, the Uighurs, and the Han Chinese. To be sure, political violence and separatism in the region had been on the rise after the end of the Cold War as resentment of Chinese rule grew among ethnic minority groups that sought more autonomy.64 But Beijing was able to use both carrots (economic development) and sticks (the “war on terror”) to maintain an uneasy peace in Xinjiang.65 This fragile equilibrium collapsed on July 5, 2009, when violent clashes between ethnic Uighurs and Han Chinese erupted in Urumqi, the capital of Xinjiang, killing several hundred people. The violence persisted afterward despite heightened security measures.66

新疆，这个位于中国西北部的省份，直到19世纪末才正式并入中国，很快就成为其最大的少数民族群体维吾尔族和汉族之间冲突的中心。诚然，冷战结束后，随着寻求更多自治权的少数民族群体对中国统治的不满日益加剧，该地区的政治暴力和分裂主义情绪一直在上升。但北京能够软硬兼施（“经济发展”），维持新疆脆弱的和平。这种脆弱的平衡在2009年7月5日被打破，当时新疆首府乌鲁木齐爆发了维吾尔族和汉族之间的暴力冲突，造成数百人死亡。尽管加强了安全措施，暴力事件仍然持续不断。

In response to the deteriorating conditions in Xinjiang, Xi opted for draconian measures to eradicate the so-called three evils—fundamentalism, separatism, and terrorism. He paid a personal visit to the region in May 2014, and in August 2016 he appointed Chen Quanguo, a hard-liner with extensive background in security, as Xinjiang's new party chief. Prior to his appointment in Xinjiang, Chen had demonstrated, as party chief in Tibet from 2011 to 2016, an ability to pacify ethnic unrest. During his tenure in Tibet, he had introduced new security measures and largely succeeded in ending a wave of self-immolations by Tibetans protesting Chinese rule.67 Xi's mandate for Chen in Xinjiang was to restore stability at all costs.

面对新疆日益恶化的局势，习近平采取了严厉措施，根除所谓的“三股势力”——原教旨主义、分裂主义和恐怖主义。他于2014年5月亲自视察新疆，并于2016年8月任命在安全领域经验丰富的强硬派陈全国为新疆委书记。在被任命为新疆委书记之前，陈全国曾在2011年至2016年担任西藏自治区委书记，展现了其平息民族动乱的能力。在西藏任职期间，他推行了新的安全措施，并基本成功地平息了藏人自焚抗议中国统治的浪潮。习近平赋予陈全国在新疆的任务是不惜一切代价恢复稳定。

Consequently, with Xi's support, Chen put more than one million ordinary Uighurs and other ethnic minorities in concentration camps, euphemistically called "vocational training schools." Local officials had complete discretion to incarcerate Uighurs in these camps. The detainees were reportedly subject to brainwashing and routine abuse.68 Simultaneously, the government adopted strict surveillance measures and restrictions on the lives of Uighurs.69

因此，在习近平的支持下，陈将超过一百万普通维吾尔族和其他少数民族民众关押在集中营中，这些集中营被委婉地称为“职业技能培训学校”。地方官员拥有完全的自由裁量权，可以随意将维吾尔族人关押在这些集中营中。据报道，被拘留者遭受了洗脑和日常虐待。与此同时，政府对维吾尔族人的生活采取了严格的监控措施和限制。

Tactically, the harsh security measures seemed to have accomplished Xi's goal of pacifying ethnic unrest in Xinjiang, judging by the near disappearance of reported acts of violence. Politically, however, China has paid dearly. Its persecution of the Uighurs, for which the West has imposed sanctions, has been labeled "genocide" by many Western countries. In terms of long-term consequences, the brutal treatment of the Uighurs will almost certainly foster more extremism and boost support for separatism in the future.

从策略上看，严厉的安全措施似乎实现了习近平平息新疆民族动乱的目标，暴力事件的报道几乎绝迹。然而，从政治上看，中国为此付出了沉重的代价。西方国家已对中国迫害维吾尔族实施制裁，许多西方国家甚至将其定性为“种族灭绝”。从长远来看，对维吾尔族的残酷对待几乎肯定会在未来助长极端主义，并增加分裂主义的支持。

When China signed an agreement with the United Kingdom in 1984 on the return of Hong Kong to China in July 1997, Deng Xiaoping pledged that the British colony would retain its economic and social systems for fifty years and enjoy a "high degree of autonomy."70 Subsequently, the NPC passed the Hong Kong "Basic Law," the city's mini constitution, in April 1990, formalizing its autonomy and China's commitment to maintaining the economic and social systems of Hong Kong for fifty years.

1984年，中国与英国签署协议，香港将于1997年7月回归中国。邓小平承诺，香港这个英国殖民地将保留其经济和社会制度五十年，并享有“高度自治”。随后，全国人民代表大会于1990年4月通过了《香港基本法》，即香港的“小宪法”，正式确立了香港的自治地位，并重申了中国对香港经济和社会制度五十年的承诺。

But the Sino-British agreement on Hong Kong and the Basic Law left two critical issues unresolved. One was democratic self-rule in Hong Kong, and the other was a National Security Law that the city's legislature was supposed to adopt after 1997. On the first issue, China made a vague promise that gradually the city's chief executive and Legislative Council would be elected through universal suffrage. After 1997 Hong Kong's chief executive was elected by an "election committee" of 1,500 unelected individuals, most of them pro-Beijing. The city's seventy-seat Legislative Council was also elected largely undemocratically, with half of its members elected directly and the other half indirectly by "functional constituencies." On the second issue, Article 23 of the Basic Law requires that Hong Kong pass its own law on national security. As the article could easily result in a law restricting the city's civil rights and freedoms, it was seen as a persistent existential threat to the "one country, two systems" model.71

但中英关于香港和《基本法》的协议遗留了两个关键问题悬而未决。一是香港的民主自治，二是香港立法会本应在1997年后通过的国家安全法。关于第一个问题，中国含糊地承诺，香港行政长官和立法会议员将逐步通过普选产生。然而，1997年后，香港行政长官是由一个由1500名未经选举产生的“选举委员会”选出的，其中大多数人亲北京。香港的70个立法会席位也大多以非民主方式选出，一半议员由直接选举产生，另一半则由“功能界别”间接选举产生。关于第二个问题，《基本法》第二十三条规定香港必须制定自己的国家安全法。由于该文章极有可能导致一项限制该市公民权利和自由的法律出台，因此被视为对“一国两制”模式的持续性生存威胁。

Yet, it would take nearly two decades before conflict over democracy and civil liberties between the CCP and the people of Hong Kong led to the death of the "one country, two systems" model. On the surface, China largely honored its part of the deal until the rise of Xi Jinping in 2012. The only significant foreshadowing of the eventual demise of the "one country, two systems" model were the mass protests against the city leadership's attempt to pass a National Security Law in 2003, which forced Hong Kong's pro-Beijing chief executive to abandon the plan. However, tensions over political rights, protection of civil rights, and identity were never far below the superficial calm.72

然而，中共与香港人民之间围绕民主和公民自由的冲突，直到近二十年后才最终导致“一国两制”模式的终结。表面上看，在2012年习近平上台之前，中国基本上履行了其在协议中的承诺。唯一预示“一国两制”最终瓦解的迹象，是2003年香港特区政府试图通过《国家安全法》时引发的大规模抗议活动，这场抗议迫使亲北京的香港特首放弃了该计划。然而，围绕政治权利、公民权利保护和身份认同的紧张局势，始终潜藏在表面的平静之下。

Shortly after Xi became CCP chief in late 2012, prodemocracy forces began to pressure Beijing more aggressively to honor its promise of universal suffrage. In March 2013 three academics called for a civil disobedience movement, "Occupy Central," the key demand of which was the replacement of Hong Kong's undemocratic electoral system with direct democratic elections. Instead of a positive response, the Chinese government issued a hard-line white paper on Hong Kong in June 2014 that flatly rejected the idea of instituting universal suffrage in the city. Most ominously, the white paper claimed that the central government has "comprehensive governing authority" over the city, a key concept that later helped legitimize Beijing's adoption of the 2020 National Security Law that effectively ended "one country, two systems" in Hong Kong.73

2012年底习近平就任中共总书记后不久，民主派力量开始更加积极地向北京施压，要求其兑现普选承诺。2013年3月，三位学者发起“占领中环”公民抗命运动，其核心诉求是以直接民主选举取代香港不民主的选举制度。然而，中国政府并未积极回应，反而于2014年6月发布了一份强硬的香港问题白皮书，断然拒绝在香港实行普选。更令人担忧的是，该白皮书声称中央政府对香港拥有“全面治理权”，这一关键概念后来成为北京通过2020年《国家安全法》的合法性依据，该法实际上终结了香港的“一国两制”。

If Beijing expected this document to pacify the demands for democracy in Hong Kong, it achieved the opposite effect. From the end of September to mid-December 2014, tens of thousands of students launched what came to be known as the "Umbrella Movement"—a series of peaceful sit-ins in the busiest section of the central part of Hong Kong. Although the movement failed to force Beijing to back down, the outpouring of public support for the demonstrators and outrage against the use of excessive force by the police became a harbinger of the far larger confrontation between Hong Kong citizens and Beijing that would take place five years later.74

如果北京期望这份文件能够平息香港民众对民主的诉求，那么它却适得其反。从2014年9月底到12月中旬，数万名学生发起了一场被称为“雨伞运动”的示威活动——在香港中心城区最繁华的地段举行了一系列和平静坐示威。尽管这场运动未能迫使北京让步，但公众对示威者的声援以及对警方过度使用武力的强烈谴责，预示着五年后香港市民与北京之间将爆发更为大规模的冲突。

The display of defiance by Hong Kong's prodemocracy activists appeared to have hardened Xi's resolve. In July 2017, at the ceremony marking the twentieth anniversary of Hong Kong's return, Xi delivered a thinly veiled threat against the city's prodemocracy forces. He warned, "Any activities that harm national sovereignty and security, challenge the power of the central government and the authority of the Basic Law, and use Hong Kong to conduct infiltration and sabotage against the mainland . . . violate our bottom line and are absolutely not permitted."75

香港民主派人士的反抗似乎更加坚定了习近平的决心。2017年7月，在香港回归二十周年纪念仪式上，习近平对香港民主派发出了隐晦的威胁。他警告说：“任何损害国家主权和安全、挑战中央权力和基本法权威、利用香港对内地进行渗透和破坏的活动……都触及了我们的底线，绝对不允许。”

Two years later, Hong Kong's prodemocracy forces tested Xi's "bottom line" when they organized mass protests against proposed legislation on extraditing Hong Kong residents to the mainland for criminal prosecution. Launched in March 2019, these protests grew progressively larger and eventually resulted in violent confrontations with the police. On several occasions, an estimated one to two million protesters marched in the streets. Clashes between police and protesters paralyzed the city, Asia's premium commercial hub, for days. This round of protests, known as the "anti-extradition" movement, ended in January 2020 after Hong Kong was locked down due to the Covid-19 pandemic.76

两年后，香港民主力量组织大规模抗议活动，反对将香港居民引渡至内地受审的立法提案，以此试探习近平的“底线”。这些抗议活动始于2019年3月，规模不断扩大，最终演变为与警方的暴力冲突。据估计，曾有数百万至两百万抗议者走上街头。警民冲突导致这座亚洲顶级商业中心瘫痪数日。这轮被称为“反引渡”运动的抗议活动，在香港因新冠疫情封城后于2020年1月结束。

The anti-extradition movement was apparently the last straw for Xi. In May 2020 the NPC passed a National Security Law for Hong Kong in a clear violation of both the technical provisions of the Basic Law (which stipulates that only the city's Legislative Council can pass such a law) and China's pledge to maintain Hong Kong's social and economic systems for fifty years. The law, which effectively guts the city's rule of law and deprives its citizens of their civil liberties, went into effect on July 1, 2020. Following implementation, Beijing dispatched its own security agents to the city as Hong Kong police, almost certainly under the direction of Beijing, arrested and charged protest organizers and civic leaders. Deng's much-vaunted "one country, two systems" model lasted a mere twenty-three years.77

反修例运动显然成了压垮习近平的最后一根稻草。2020年5月，全国人大通过了香港国安法，这明显违反了《基本法》的技术性规定（该法规定只有香港立法会才能通过此类法律）以及中国对香港社会经济制度五十年的承诺。该法实际上摧毁了香港的法治，剥夺了香港市民的公民自由，并于2020年7月1日生效。法实施后，北京向香港派遣了安全人员，而香港警方几乎可以肯定是在北京的指示下逮捕并起诉了抗议组织者和公民领袖。邓小平大肆宣扬的“一国两制”模式仅仅维持了二十三年。

Although Xi crushed the prodemocracy movement in Hong Kong, the costs for China, the CCP, and Xi himself were horrific. The United States terminated its preferential treatment for the city. The end of the rule of law in Hong Kong also fatally damaged the city's status as a center of commerce, resulting in the exodus of Western businesses and talent to other parts of Asia, mostly Singapore.78 Internationally, China lost its credibility. The crackdown in Hong Kong, seen widely as unnecessary, excessive, and self-destructive, served only to reinforce the view that a powerful autocratic China cannot be trusted and must be confronted.

尽管习近平镇压了香港的民主运动，但中国、中共以及习近平本人为此付出了惨痛的代价。美国终止了对香港的特殊待遇。香港法治的终结也严重损害了其作为商业中心的地位，导致西方企业和人才大量外流至亚洲其他地区，其中大部分流向了新加坡。在国际上，中国的信誉也随之丧失。这场被广泛认为不必要、过度且自毁的香港镇压行动，反而更加强化了人们对一个强大的专制中国不可信赖、必须与之对抗的看法。





What Made the Return of Totalitarian Rule Possible





是什么让极权统治的回归成为可能？


Few could have imagined the transformative changes Xi brought about almost single-handedly within a decade of rising to the top. The reversion to neo-Stalinist rule is all the more remarkable—and puzzling—given Xi's weak powerbase and the massive socioeconomic modernization China experienced in the post-Mao era. In all likelihood, Xi himself probably did not anticipate the relative ease with which he could dismantle the post-Tiananmen order and restore a regime bearing the essential characteristics of neo-Stalinism: personalistic rule, permanent purges, ruthless repression, and an expansionist foreign policy.

很少有人能预料到，习近平在短短十年内几乎凭借一己之力就带来了翻天覆地的变化。考虑到习近平薄弱的权力基础以及中国在后毛泽东时代经历的大规模社会经济现代化，他倒退回新斯大林主义统治就显得更加引人注目，也更加令人费解。习近平本人很可能也没有预料到，他能够如此轻易地瓦解天安门事件后的秩序，并重建一个具有新斯大林主义本质特征的政权：个人主义统治、持续不断的清洗、残酷镇压以及扩张主义的外交政策。

Xi could reconstruct a neo-Stalinist order against ostensibly poor odds primarily because the regime's totalitarian institutional framework had remained largely intact in spite of the post-Mao economic reforms and opening to the West. Indeed, even a cursory comparison between China in 1979 and China in 2012 shows that foundational institutions of totalitarianism remained essentially untouched by the country's "reform and opening." Most critically, the institutional pillar of totalitarianism—a Leninist party-state—was completely preserved. The CCP's closed and hierarchical organizational structure and procedures for leadership selection were not fundamentally different in 2012 from what they were in 1979. Despite attempts to separate the party from the state, the party remained deeply entrenched in and dominant over the state. Its organizational penetration of Chinese society, down to the neighborhood and village levels, had deepened and expanded rather than withering, allowing the party to retain its unrivaled capacities for social control and political mobilization.

习近平之所以能够在看似不利的情况下重建新斯大林主义秩序，主要原因在于，尽管后毛泽东时代的经济改革和对外开放取得了进展，但该政权的极权主义制度框架却基本保持完整。事实上，即使对1979年的中国和2012年的中国进行粗略的比较，也能看出极权主义的基础制度基本上没有受到中国“改革开放”的影响。最关键的是，极权主义的制度支柱——列宁主义的党国体制——被完整地保留了下来。中共封闭的等级制组织结构和领导人选拔程序在2012年与1979年并无本质区别。尽管中共试图将党与国家分离，但它仍然深深扎根于国家之中，并凌驾于国家之上。其对中国社会，乃至社区和乡村层面的组织渗透非但没有减弱，反而更加深入和广泛，这使得中共得以保持其无与伦比的社会控制和政治动员能力。

Almost equally critical was the party's control of instruments of state violence without any constitutional or legal constraints. To be sure, the indiscriminate mass terror of the Mao era was replaced by selective repression. But the party had at its disposal the military, the secret police, and a vast surveillance apparatus to guard its political monopoly. When necessary, as demonstrated by the crackdown on the Tiananmen movement and the suppression of the Falungong spiritual group, the party could mobilize state violence to crush any challenges to its power. The revival of totalitarianism under Xi would not have been possible without a coercive apparatus that received massive state investments during the post-Tiananmen era.79

同样至关重要的是，党对国家暴力工具的控制不受任何宪法或法律约束。诚然，毛泽东时代不分青红皂白的大规模恐怖统治已被选择性镇压所取代。但党仍然拥有军队、秘密警察和庞大的监控体系来维护其政治垄断地位。必要时，正如镇压天安门运动和打压法轮功精神团体所表明的那样，党可以动用国家暴力来粉碎任何对其权力的挑战。如果没有在后天安门时代获得国家巨额投资的强制机器，习近平领导下的极权主义复兴是不可能实现的。

Although the post-Mao reforms eroded the regime's capacity to control the economy and its access to information, the party-state could easily reassert its control when necessary. Economically, the regime retained the "commanding heights" of the economy, such as the financial system, energy, transportation, and telecom services. It also monopolized ownership of land and wielded immense regulatory power. Aware of the threats posed by free flows of information, the party maintained strict control of the media and, when confronted by the internet, quickly adopted effective countermeasures to neutralize the information revolution.80

尽管后毛泽东时代的改革削弱了政权对经济的控制能力及其获取信息的渠道，但党国在必要时仍能轻易地重新掌控局面。在经济方面，政权仍然掌控着经济的“制高点”，例如金融体系、能源、交通运输和电信服务。它还垄断了土地所有权，并拥有巨大的监管权力。意识到信息自由流动带来的威胁，党对媒体实行严格控制，并在面对互联网时迅速采取有效措施来遏制信息革命。

Prior to Xi's rise, three features of a classic totalitarian regime were missing: One was a domineering totalitarian leader. But that was largely a historical accident because the fragile balance of power at the top prevented the reemergence of a Stalinist or Maoist dictator. Also missing were the permanent purges, thanks to the collective leadership maintained by the same balance of power. The third missing feature was an official ideology legitimating party rule. Although the CCP never formally abandoned its Communist ideology, in reality the ideology atrophied due to the general worldwide failure of Communist regimes and Mao's disastrous rule. Economic performance became the party's real source of legitimacy, while pragmatism, not orthodox ideology, dictated policy.

在习近平崛起之前，典型的极权政权缺少三个特征：一是专横跋扈的极权领袖。但这很大程度上是历史的偶然，因为高层脆弱的权力平衡阻止了斯大林式或毛泽东式独裁者的再次出现。二是持续不断的清洗，这也得益于同样的权力平衡所维系的集体领导。第三个缺失的特征是官方意识形态，它为党的统治提供了合法性。尽管中共从未正式放弃其共产主义意识形态，但实际上，由于世界范围内共产主义政权的普遍失败以及毛泽东灾难性的统治，这种意识形态已经衰落。经济表现成为党的真正合法性来源，而政策的制定则更多地依赖于实用主义，而非正统的意识形态。

Of these three missing features of classic totalitarianism, the first two could be easily revived, as demonstrated by Xi's record. Once the fragile balance of power ceased to exist, the party had no means to prevent a ruthless leader from restoring one-man rule and reviving permanent purges to terrorize the party. Reinvigorating the orthodox Communist ideology was, by comparison, a far more challenging undertaking, even for Xi, because it held little appeal to a party and a society thoroughly secularized by the socioeconomic changes and the post-Mao era contacts with the outside world.

经典极权主义缺失的这三个特征中，前两个很容易恢复，习近平的所作所为就证明了这一点。一旦脆弱的权力平衡不复存在，党就无力阻止一位冷酷无情的领导人恢复一人统治，并恢复持续不断的清洗以恐吓党员。相比之下，重振正统的共产主义意识形态则是一项更为艰巨的任务，即使对习近平而言也是如此，因为对于一个因社会经济变革和后毛泽东时代与外部世界的接触而彻底世俗化的党和社会而言，这种意识形态几乎没有任何吸引力。

Ironically, although Xi reversed Deng's policy of reform and opening, he owes much of his success to Deng's commitment to one-party rule and to his personal political interests. In saving the party from Mao's disastrous rule, Deng's consistent strategy was to change economic policy without endangering one-party rule. The most important of his "four cardinal principles" is the political supremacy of the party. For Deng, reform and opening were simply the means to save the CCP and to perpetuate its rule. Specifically, Deng left two political legacies that later greatly facilitated Xi's efforts to restore totalitarian rule. The first was his unwavering opposition to any political reform or to any ideological liberalization that might weaken party rule or expose its dark side. Deng's conservatism precluded a thorough reckoning of the disasters of the Maoist era or a liberalization that could lead to a stronger civil society or had the potential to resist any reversion to totalitarian rule. Most critically, Deng's purge of Hu Yaobang in 1987 and Zhao Ziyang in 1989 decimated the liberals in the party and decisively shifted the balance of power in favor of the hard-liners.

具有讽刺意味的是，尽管习近平推翻了邓小平的改革开放政策，但他的成功很大程度上要归功于邓小平对一党专政的坚持以及他个人的政治利益。为了将党从毛泽东灾难性的统治中拯救出来，邓小平一贯的策略是在不危及一党专政的前提下改变经济政策。他“四大原则”中最重要的是党的政治至上。对邓小平而言，改革开放仅仅是拯救中共并延续其统治的手段。具体来说，邓小平留下的两项政治遗产，后来极大地便利了习近平恢复极权统治的努力。首先，他坚决反对任何可能削弱党的统治或暴露其阴暗面的政治改革或意识形态自由化。邓小平的保守主义阻碍了对毛泽东时代灾难的彻底反思，也阻碍了可能促进公民社会发展或有可能抵制任何回归极权统治的自由化进程。最关键的是，邓小平在 1987 年清洗胡耀邦，在 1989 年清洗赵紫阳，严重削弱了党内的自由派，并决定性地改变了权力平衡，使之有利于强硬派。

The second legacy was Deng's flawed reforms to preserve collective leadership and prevent the return of a Mao-like figure. The formal provisions on term limits, mandatory retirement, and rights of party members were intentionally left vague and impossible to enforce. For example, the only explicit term limit was that imposed on the state president, the least important of the three positions held by the regime's top leader (the other two being the general secretary and the chairman of the CMC). But as the party made it easy to change the constitution, this limit too could be abolished without much trouble, as Xi did in 2018. Deng himself set a bad example by violating the rules he tried to establish. He held on to power despite his advanced age and lack of formal titles. He made a mockery of the party's formal procedures by holding private meetings with senior leaders in his home rather than allowing the Politburo Standing Committee to act in its capacity as the party's top decision-making body. His most momentous decisions were made mostly by himself or in consultation with a small number of aging revolutionaries. Most important, although Deng paid lip-service to "democratic political life within the party," he made no attempt to establish inner-party democracy, depriving the party of a mechanism to hold its leaders accountable and to block the return of a Mao-like figure.

邓小平留下的第二个遗产是他为维护集体领导、防止毛泽东式人物复辟而推行的改革，但这些改革存在缺陷。关于任期限制、强制退休和党员权利的正式规定被刻意模糊化，使其难以执行。例如，唯一明确的任期限制是针对国家主席的，而国家主席是政权最高领导人三个职位中最不重要的（另外两个职位是中央总书记和中央军委主席）。但由于党章修改的便利性，这一限制也很容易被废除，正如习近平在2018年所做的那样。邓小平本人也树立了一个坏榜样，他违反了自己试图建立的规则。尽管年事已高且没有正式头衔，他仍然牢牢把持着权力。他没有让政治局常委履行其作为党的最高决策机构的职责，而是私下与高级领导人举行会议，这无疑是对党的正式程序的嘲弄。他最重要的决策大多是由他自己做出的，或者只是与少数几位年迈的革命者商议后做出的。最重要的是，尽管邓小平口头上支持“党内民主政治生活”，但他并没有尝试建立党内民主，这使得党失去了追究领导人责任和阻止毛泽东式人物回归的机制。

The survival of collective leadership and adherence to the procedures and norms of succession in the post-Deng era created the deceptive impression that Deng's reforms were effective and durable. Overlooked was the difficulty, if not the impossibility, of institutionalizing politics in an autocracy.81 Indeed, the inherent flaws of Deng's reforms enabled Xi to amass the power of a totalitarian leader without any real opposition.

邓小平之后集体领导制度的延续以及对权力交接程序和规范的恪守，给人一种错觉，仿佛邓小平的改革卓有成效且持久。然而，人们却忽略了在专制政体中实现政治制度化的难度，甚至可以说是不可能。事实上，邓小平改革的固有缺陷使得习近平得以在几乎没有任何真正反对的情况下，攫取极权统治者的权力。





Peaking Xi?





习近平达到巅峰了吗？


Despite Xi's success in reviving totalitarian rule, signs that his neo-Stalinist agenda had run its course began to emerge toward the end of his second term. The initial pushback against him came from the United States in 2018 when Donald Trump launched a trade war against China. Although Trump was motivated less by grand geopolitical designs than by his personal political interests, the US-China trade war quickly led to a comprehensive deterioration of US-China relations that immediately escalated to a new cold war.

尽管习近平成功地复兴了极权统治，但在其第二个任期末期，他的新斯大林主义议程已然走向终结的迹象开始显现。最初对他的反击来自美国，2018年唐纳德·特朗普对中国发动了贸易战。尽管特朗普的动机与其说是出于宏大的地缘政治考量，不如说是出于其个人政治利益，但这场美中贸易战迅速导致美中关系全面恶化，并立即升级为一场新的冷战。

The Covid-19 pandemic that struck China in late December 2019 marked the beginning of the unraveling of Xi's neo-Stalinist agenda on the domestic front. Although the initial success of the Chinese government in containing the pandemic gave the party a political boost, the emergence of a more infectious viral variant in 2022 rendered Xi's zero-Covid strategy ineffective. Instead of abandoning this untenable approach, Xi stuck to it, most likely because he did not want to see an explosive rise in the number of infections and deaths ahead of the Twentieth Party Congress, scheduled for the fall of 2022 (which was to grant him a third term). Nationwide lockdowns resulted in a steep decline in economic activities and stoked public anger. By late November 2022, a month after the conclusion of the party congress, the Chinese public had had enough. After a fire killed ten people in their apartments under lockdown in Urumqi on November 24, thousands of young students and professionals spontaneously began demonstrating in more than a dozen cities, some even shouting "Xi Jinping, step down!"82 Apparently shocked by this outburst of public anger, Xi relented and ordered an immediate end to zero-Covid, marking his first humiliating retreat from a demonstrably failed policy.83

2019年12月底席卷中国的新冠疫情标志着习近平在国内推行的新斯大林主义议程开始瓦解。尽管中国政府在控制疫情方面取得的初步成功为党带来了政治优势，但2022年更具传染性的病毒变种的出现，使得习近平的“清零”战略失效。习近平非但没有放弃这一行不通的策略，反而坚持己见，很可能是因为他不想在2022年秋季召开的中共二十大（旨在让他连任第三届）之前看到感染和死亡人数的爆炸性增长。全国范围内的封锁导致经济活动急剧下滑，并激起了公众的愤怒。到2022年11月底，也就是中共二十大闭幕一个月后，中国民众已经忍无可忍。 11月24日，乌鲁木齐一栋公寓楼发生火灾，造成10人死亡，此前该市一直处于封锁状态。此后，数千名青年学生和专业人士自发在十几个城市举行示威游行，一些人甚至高喊“习近平下台！”。显然，习近平被这股民愤所震惊，被迫让步，下令立即结束“清零”政策，这标志着他首次在明显失败的政策上做出屈辱性的让步。

But that may have been too late, as far as the Chinese economy was concerned. Instead of a robust recovery that failed to materialize after the end of zero-Covid, the economy struggled on all fronts, with an imploding real estate sector, slumping exports, falling investment, and high youth unemployment.84 To be sure, most of the factors responsible for China's economic difficulties, such as high levels of debt, the gigantic real estate bubble, and deteriorating relations with the West, had preceded the pandemic. Nevertheless, these problems were exacerbated by Xi's zero-Covid policy. Its restrictions on international travel made normal business activities almost impossible, frequently disrupted supply chains, and led to the closure of many small businesses.

但就中国经济而言，这或许为时已晚。疫情结束后，中国经济并未如预期般强劲复苏，反而陷入各方面困境：房地产市场崩盘、出口下滑、投资减少、青年失业率居高不下。诚然，导致中国经济困境的诸多因素，例如高额债务、巨大的房地产泡沫以及与西方关系恶化，大多在疫情爆发前就已存在。然而，习近平的疫情政策加剧了这些问题。其对国际旅行的限制几乎使正常的商业活动无法开展，供应链频频中断，并导致众多小型企业倒闭。

The persistent economic weaknesses may derail Xi's agenda of strengthening one-party rule at home and surpassing the United States as the world's largest economy. Dwindling financial resources could force him to curtail spending on his pet projects, such as military modernization, technological self-sufficiency, and "common prosperity," a plan to reduce socioeconomic inequality. Tighter budgets might also limit the party's ability to distribute resources to its favored interest groups, such as SOEs and key provinces. Protracted slow growth will result in stagnant standards of living and undermine the confidence of both the private sector and foreign investors in China's economic future. The performance legitimacy that has undergirded party rule since the Tiananmen crackdown will likely evaporate.

持续的经济疲软可能会阻碍习近平在国内巩固一党专政、超越美国成为世界最大经济体的计划。财政资源的日益匮乏可能迫使他削减其重点项目的支出，例如军事现代化、技术自给自足以及旨在缩小社会经济差距的“共同繁荣”计划。预算紧缩也可能限制党向其所青睐的利益集团（例如国有企业和重点省份）分配资源的能力。长期低迷的经济增长将导致生活水平停滞不前，并削弱私营部门和外国投资者对中国经济前景的信心。自天安门事件以来支撑党执政的政绩合法性很可能就此瓦解。

Judging by his response to China's economic difficulties, Xi seems to have no new ideas to sustain his neo-Stalinist project, except for placing national security at the top of the party's priorities. Instead of launching economic initiatives to rekindle growth, Xi has approved a series of measures, such as passage of a broad anti-espionage law and a campaign to catch foreign spies in 2023, succeeding only to further alienate Western investors and reinforce the pessimism of private entrepreneurs. Politically, Xi may benefit, at least in the short term, by underscoring the danger of hostile foreign forces and blaming Washington's economic cold war for China's problems. In the long run, however, the continuation of a security-centered survival strategy will make economic stagnation more likely, forcing Xi to depend even more on repression to keep the party—and himself—in power.
