从习近平对中国经济困境的应对来看，除了将国家安全置于党的首要位置之外，他似乎没有其他新思路来支撑其新斯大林主义路线。习近平没有推出任何刺激经济增长的举措，而是批准了一系列措施，例如通过一项范围广泛的反间谍法，以及在2023年开展打击外国间谍的行动，但这些措施最终只会进一步疏远西方投资者，并加剧私营企业家的悲观情绪。在政治上，习近平或许能在短期内通过强调敌对外国势力的威胁，并将中国的问题归咎于华盛顿的经济冷战而获益。然而，从长远来看，继续奉行以安全为中心的生存战略只会增加经济停滞的可能性，迫使习近平更加依赖镇压手段来维持党的统治——以及他自身的权力。







7 End of the Chinese Economic Miracle

7 中国经济奇迹的终结


THE DETERIORATION of the Chinese economy shortly after the country emerged from its Covid-19 lockdowns in December 2022 caught both Chinese leaders and outside observers by surprise. Weighed down by the collapse of the largest real estate bubble in history, heavily indebted local governments and SOEs, and geopolitical tensions, China struggled to regain the same rate of growth prior to the pandemic. But in retrospect, the end of the Chinese economic miracle in the Xi Jinping era was a foregone conclusion. The party's failure to implement more radical market-oriented reforms in the Hu Jintao era led to a gradual erosion of overall efficiency and diminished the country's growth prospects. As explained in chapters 3 and 4, stagnation was the logical outcome of a "trapped transition"—the progressive loss of the political incentives to pursue reform by a neo-authoritarian regime. When Xi Jinping succeeded in reviving China's dormant totalitarian institutions, the adoption of radical pro-market reforms to rejuvenate growth would be ideologically and politically impossible, thus spelling the end of the economic miracle.

2022年12月，中国刚刚解除新冠疫情封锁措施，经济便迅速恶化，这令中国领导人和外界观察人士都感到措手不及。历史上最大的房地产泡沫破裂、地方政府和国有企业负债累累以及地缘政治紧张局势，都给中国经济带来了沉重的负担，使其难以恢复到疫情前的增长速度。但事后看来，习近平时代中国经济奇迹的终结其实早已注定。胡锦涛时代，中共未能推行更加激进的市场化改革，导致整体效率逐渐下降，并削弱了国家的增长前景。正如本书第三章和第四章所述，经济停滞是“转型困境”的必然结果——即新威权政权逐渐丧失推行改革的政治动力。当习近平成功复兴中国沉寂已久的极权体制后，采取激进的亲市场改革来重振经济增长在意识形态和政治上都是不可能的，这标志着经济奇迹的终结。

Ideologically, Xi's brand of neo-Stalinist rule would further elevate the political supremacy of the party, resulting in the strengthening of the party-state's direct control of the economy and the extension of its hold on the private sector. Theoretically, a promising course of reform might exist on paper, as evidenced by sensible prescriptions well-known to Chinese leaders.1 However, such economic reforms would be impracticable without accompanying political reforms. By the time Xi ascended to the top, powerful interests benefiting from the systemic inefficiencies of China's partially reformed economy—such as families of senior officials and their cronies in the business world, local government officials, state-owned enterprises and, most important, the party itself—would resist these reforms that threatened their power and privileges. It is worth repeating that these political forces were themselves the inevitable consequences of the inherent limitations of Dengist neo-authoritarianism. With favorable one-off structural factors, economic development under one-party rule might score impressive early results but would eventually lose steam and stagnate, as happened in the Xi era.

从意识形态上看，习近平的新斯大林主义统治将进一步提升党的政治至高地位，从而加强党国对经济的直接控制，并扩大其对私营部门的控制。理论上，改革的前景或许在纸面上存在，中国领导人熟知的合理方案也印证了这一点。然而，若没有相应的政治改革，此类经济改革将难以实施。在习近平掌权之时，那些从中国部分改革后的经济体制弊端中获益的强大利益集团——例如高级官员的家族及其在商界的亲信、地方政府官员、国有企业，以及最重要的，党本身——将会抵制这些威胁到其权力和特权的改革。值得重申的是，这些政治力量本身就是邓小平新威权主义固有局限性的必然结果。在有利的一次性结构性因素的影响下，一党专政下的经济发展可能会在初期取得令人瞩目的成果，但最终会失去动力并停滞不前，就像习近平时代发生的那样。





The Economy Xi Inherited





习近平继承的经济


Growth started sputtering even before Xi assumed power in late 2012. Economic output recorded its last double-digit growth of 10.2 percent in 2010. In 2012 growth had slowed to 8.1 percent.2 To be sure, sustaining double-digit growth for an economy of $8.5 trillion in 2012 would be no easy feat. Reversion to the mean—a fall in growth rates that brings the expansion of output to the historical average—is the law of economics that applies to China in the same way as it does to all economies.3 However, China's apparent entry into a period of moderate growth, what its leaders preferred to call "the new normal," was accompanied by several economic abnormalities that compounded the challenges faced by the CCP in its attempts to sustain sufficient dynamism and turn China into a high-income economy.

早在习近平2012年底上台之前，经济增长就已经开始放缓。经济产出最后一次两位数增长是在2010年，当时增速为10.2%。2012年，增速已放缓至8.1%。2 诚然，对于2012年经济规模达8.5万亿美元的中国来说，维持两位数增长绝非易事。均值回归——即增长率下降，最终使产出扩张回归历史平均水平——是适用于中国和其他所有经济体的经济规律。3 然而，中国表面上进入了温和增长时期，其领导人更愿意称之为“新常态”，但与此同时，也出现了一些经济异常现象，这些现象加剧了中共在维持足够活力和将中国打造成为高收入经济体方面所面临的挑战。

Perhaps the most important economic anomaly—and a persistent constraint on the economy—was the structural imbalance that emerged in the post-Tiananmen period and remained uncorrected throughout the Hu Jintao era. Specifically, economic growth was excessively reliant on investment, a dependency that inevitably results in diminishing returns and overcapacity. If anything, this macroeconomic imbalance worsened under Hu. At the end of 2002, when Hu became party chief, investment accounted for about 38 percent of GDP. By 2012, when Xi succeeded Hu, investment had risen to 48 percent of GDP.4 Although Hu was able to muddle through despite the growing macroeconomic imbalance, the odds that Xi would be able to do so during the period of “the new normal” appeared to be far less favorable. He did not enjoy many of the advantages of the Hu regime, such as relatively low levels of debt, a massive expansion of exports due to China's WTO entry, and healthy demographics, just to mention a few.

或许最重要的经济异常现象——也是对经济发展持续制约的因素——是天安门事件后出现并在胡锦涛时代始终未得到纠正的结构性失衡。具体而言，经济增长过度依赖投资，这种依赖必然导致收益递减和产能过剩。胡锦涛执政期间，这种宏观经济失衡反而加剧。2002年底胡锦涛就任党总书记时，投资约占GDP的38%。到2012年习近平接替胡锦涛时，投资已升至GDP的48%。尽管胡锦涛能够勉强应对日益严重的宏观经济失衡，但习近平在“新常态”下能否做到这一点似乎远没有那么乐观。他没有享有胡锦涛执政时期的诸多优势，例如相对较低的债务水平、加入世贸组织后出口的大幅增长以及健康的人口结构等等。

In addition to the worsening macroeconomic imbalances, another serious and potentially perilous obstacle confronting Xi was the rapidly rising level of debt following China's credit-fueled stimulus in response to the 2008 global financial crisis. Total outstanding credit to the nonfinancial sector stood at 192 percent of GDP at the end of 2012. By comparison, when Hu became party chief a decade earlier, the amount of debt was 142 percent of GDP. Under Xi, this ratio would grow even higher, reaching 297 percent of GDP by the end of 2022. Debt incurred by the state (mostly local governments) was 35 percent of GDP at the end of 2012 and would rise to 78 percent of GDP by 2022. At the end of 2012, the leverage of companies, mostly SOEs, was at 128 percent of GDP; ten years later it reached 158 percent of GDP.5

除了日益恶化的宏观经济失衡之外，习近平面临的另一个严重且潜在的危险障碍是，在2008年全球金融危机后，中国采取信贷刺激措施，导致债务水平迅速攀升。截至2012年底，非金融部门未偿信贷总额占GDP的192%。相比之下，十年前胡锦涛担任中共中央总书记时，债务占GDP的142%。在习近平的领导下，这一比例将进一步攀升，到2022年底将达到GDP的297%。2012年底，国家（主要是地方政府）债务占GDP的35%，预计到2022年将升至GDP的78%。2012年底，企业（主要是国有企业）杠杆率为GDP的128%；十年后，这一比例达到GDP的158%。

The housing bubble, the third economic challenge confronting Xi, was at an early stage in 2012. Residential housing had boomed under Hu. In 2003 about 2.6 billion square meters of floor space were under construction; by 2012, the figure was roughly four times that amount, at 9.86 billion square meters.6

房地产泡沫是习近平面临的第三项经济挑战，2012年时它还处于早期阶段。胡锦涛执政时期，住宅建设蓬勃发展。2003年，在建住宅建筑面积约为26亿平方米；到2012年，这一数字约为当时的四倍，达到98.6亿平方米。

The last major danger lurking on the horizon was the fraying of relations with China's main trading partners in the West as a result of the sustained high trade deficits. America's bilateral merchandise trade deficit with China ballooned from $124 billion in 2003 to $315 billion in 2012.7 In the same period, the European Union's bilateral merchandise trade deficit with China nearly doubled, from $74 billion to $130 billion.8 Even though bilateral trade imbalances do not necessarily mean that one of the parties has been harmed, persistently high deficit levels are often seen as evidence of unfair trade practices perpetuated by the party recording a surplus. In the case of Sino-American trade, high imbalances in China's favor were exploited successfully by Donald Trump to win the support of blue-collar workers in the US rust belt, igniting a US-China trade war in 2018.9

最后一个潜伏在地平线上的主要危险是，由于持续的高额贸易逆差，中国与西方主要贸易伙伴的关系可能出现恶化。美国对华双边商品贸易逆差从2003年的1240亿美元飙升至2012年的3150亿美元。同期，欧盟对华双边商品贸易逆差几乎翻了一番，从740亿美元增至1300亿美元。尽管双边贸易失衡并不一定意味着一方遭受损失，但持续的高逆差水平通常被视为顺差方实施不公平贸易行为的证据。以中美贸易为例，唐纳德·特朗普成功利用了对中国有利的严重贸易失衡，赢得了美国“铁锈地带”蓝领工人的支持，从而在2018年引发了美中贸易战。

By 2012, most of the favorable structural and political factors that had earlier propelled double-digit growth had either dissipated or were weakening. The pool of cheap labor from the rural areas was declining, causing wages to rise rapidly. In the manufacturing sector, the average wage in 2012 was 2.3 times higher than it had been in 2002 in real terms.10 The population was also aging. About 94 million people (7.3 percent of the population) were aged 65 or older in 2002. Ten years later, the country had 127 million people aged 65 or older (9.4 percent of the population). In 2021 over 200 million, or 14.2 percent of the population, would be aged 65 or older.11 The lack of reform during the Hu period and the shift of resources to the real estate sector and to unproductive infrastructure due to the 2009 stimulus package caused a precipitous fall in productivity.12

到2012年，此前推动两位数增长的大部分有利结构性和政治性因素要么已经消失，要么正在减弱。来自农村地区的廉价劳动力减少，导致工资快速上涨。在制造业，2012年的平均工资实际水平是2002年的2.3倍。人口老龄化问题也日益严重。2002年，65岁及以上的人口约为9400万（占总人口的7.3%）。十年后，这一数字上升至1.27亿（占总人口的9.4%）。到2021年，超过2亿人口，即14.2%的人口，将年满65岁或以上。11 胡锦涛时期缺乏改革，以及2009年刺激计划导致资源向房地产行业和非生产性基础设施转移，造成生产率急剧下降。12

This summary of the Chinese economy in late 2012 reveals serious risks, such as macroeconomic imbalances, high and growing levels of debt, an incipient housing bubble, and deteriorating ties with its major trading partners. Although the Chinese government put a positive spin on the slowing growth, claiming that the country had entered "the new normal" phase of development, these risks threatened to make the new normal anything but normal. Economic stagnation could easily result from the chronic lack of consumption-driven demand and the overreliance on one sector, i.e., housing, as a driver of growth. The high debt levels could trigger a financial crisis, and the sustained trade imbalances could ignite trade wars. Indeed, these economic difficulties would culminate, during Xi's third term, in a prolonged economic slump marked by high youth unemployment, a colossal real estate collapse, and deflation.

这份对2012年末中国经济的总结揭示了诸多严重风险，例如宏观经济失衡、高企且不断增长的债务水平、萌芽中的房地产泡沫以及与主要贸易伙伴关系的恶化。尽管中国政府对经济增长放缓进行了积极解读，声称中国已进入“新常态”发展阶段，但这些风险却有可能使所谓的“新常态”远非正常。长期缺乏消费驱动型需求以及过度依赖单一行业（即房地产）作为增长引擎，极易导致经济停滞。高额债务可能引发金融危机，而持续的贸易失衡则可能引发贸易战。事实上，在习近平的第三个任期内，这些经济困境最终导致了长期的经济衰退，其特征是青年失业率居高不下、房地产市场崩盘以及通货紧缩。





Unkept Promises





未兑现的承诺


At the Third Plenum of the Eighteenth Central Committee in November 2013, Xi unveiled a sixty-point reform plan, apparently to establish his credentials as a reformer. Despite its title, "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Some Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Deepening the Reform," Xi's blueprint is notable for its contradictions and incompatible objectives.13 Rhetorically, the decision seems to have made an ideological breakthrough by stating: "We must deepen economic system reform by centering on the decisive role of the market in allocating resources." Previously, the party had allowed the market to play only a role that was subordinate to that of the state. However, this ideological framing contradicts the decision's insistence that in China's economic system the state-owned sector is the main entity (zhuti), with economic actors of other ownership developing side by side. To underscore its determination to maintain the dominance of the state-owned sector, the decision states: "We must unwervingly consolidate and develop the public economy, persist in the dominant position of public ownership, give full play to the leading role of the state-owned sector, and continuously increase its vitality, controlling force and influence. We must unwaveringly encourage, support and guide the development of the nonpublic sector, and stimulate its dynamism and creativity." However convoluted, the ideological formulation in the decision leaves an unmistakable impression that the party was seeking to maintain an economic system based on state ownership, with nonstate economic entities playing a subordinate role.

2013年11月，在中共十八届三中全会上，习近平公布了一项六十点改革方案，显然是为了确立其改革者的形象。尽管该方案名为《中共中央关于全面深化改革若干重大问题的决定》，但习近平的方案却因其矛盾之处和目标上的冲突而引人注目。从修辞上看，该决定似乎在意识形态上取得了突破，指出：“我们必须以市场在资源配置中的决定性作用为中心，深化经济体制改革。”此前，中共一直允许市场发挥从属于国家的作用。然而，这种意识形态框架与该决定坚持认为国有企业是中国经济体制的主体（主力），其他所有制经济主体与之并存的观点相矛盾。为了强调其维护国有经济主导地位的决心，该决定指出：“我们必须坚定不移地巩固和发展公有经济，坚持公有制的主导地位，充分发挥国有经济的领导作用，不断增强国有经济的活力、控制力和影响力。我们必须坚定不移地鼓励、支持和引导非公有经济的发展，激发其活力和创造力。” 尽管措辞复杂，但该决定的意识形态表述无疑给人留下了深刻的印象，即党试图维持以国有制为基础的经济体制，非国有经济实体则处于从属地位。

Substantively, the decision consists of two separate packages of "reform." One package addresses the flaws in the economy (such as the state-owned enterprises, the fiscal system, the financial sector, and so forth) and the delivery of public services. The other package seeks institutional changes in state institutions (the military, the legal system, and the bureaucracy).

实质上，该决定包含两套独立的“改革”方案。一套方案着眼于经济（例如国有企业、财政体系、金融部门等）和公共服务供给方面的缺陷。另一套方案则寻求对国家机构（军队、司法系统和官僚机构）进行制度性改革。

At first glance, the proposed package of economic reforms seems more radical than any of the previous reforms announced by the party in the post-Tiananmen era. For example, it proposes land reform that will benefit farmers, a fiscal reform that will raise local revenues and increase the provision of social services, price reform that will liberalize energy, utility, telecom, and transportation markets, an opening up of the financial sector to private firms, and taking rapid steps in the direction of interest and currency liberalization. Unfortunately, few of these reforms were implemented in subsequent years. If anything, the party reversed course and, instead of allowing the market to play a "decisive role," brought back the state at the expense of the private sector.14

乍看之下，这套经济改革方案似乎比中共在后天安门时代宣布的任何改革都更为激进。例如，它提议进行有利于农民的土地改革，进行增加地方财政收入和扩大社会服务供给的财政改革，进行价格改革以开放能源、公用事业、电信和交通运输市场，向私营企业开放金融领域，并迅速推进利率和货币自由化。然而，不幸的是，这些改革措施在随后的几年里鲜有落实。不仅如此，中共还改变了方向，非但没有让市场发挥“决定性作用”，反而以牺牲私营部门为代价，重新赋予国家权力。

The other package seeks to strengthen the party and its control over the state. The most notable proposals were the establishment of the CCP National Security Commission, the restructuring of the military, and tighter social controls (cybersecurity, censorship, and neighborhood-level surveillance through "grid management"). Unlike the unfulfilled economic reform promises, these measures were fully implemented during Xi's first term.

另一项改革方案旨在加强党的权力和对国家的控制。其中最引人注目的提议包括成立中共国家安全委员会、改革军队以及加强社会管控（网络安全、审查制度以及通过“网格化管理”进行社区层面的监控）。与未能兑现的经济改革承诺不同，这些措施在习近平第一任期内得到了全面落实。

Xi abandoned his economic reform plan but adhered to his blueprint to strengthen the party-state for three probable reasons. The first is the fundamental incompatibility of a fully marketized economy with the supremacy of a Leninist regime, whereby any loss of control over economic activities carries an unacceptable risk of ceding political power to economic and social forces that might underwrite or become organized opposition. This is the same dilemma that had confronted Xi's predecessors. Like them, Xi simply could not square the circle and therefore had to forgo whatever ambitions he might have had to "comprehensively deepen" reform.

习近平放弃了经济改革计划，但坚持强化党国体制的蓝图，这很可能有三个原因。首先，完全市场化的经济与列宁主义政权的至高无上根本无法兼容，任何对经济活动的失控都可能导致政治权力拱手让给经济和社会力量，而这些力量可能成为反对派的幕后推手或组织起来。习近平的前任们也面临着同样的困境。和他们一样，习近平也无法兼顾两者，因此不得不放弃他原本可能怀有的“全面深化”改革的雄心壮志。

The second factor is the combination of practical difficulties and political resistance from actors and groups that had benefited from the status quo. Some reforms, such as financial sector reforms, currency liberalization, strengthening of the social safety net, and restructuring of central-local fiscal relations, would be complex and challenging in terms of technical knowledge, resource requirements, and political opposition. For example, expanding local fiscal revenue by levying a property tax would encounter strong resistance from urban residents.

第二个因素是实际操作上的困难以及既得利益者和既得利益群体的政治阻力。一些改革，例如金融部门改革、货币自由化、加强社会保障体系以及重组中央与地方财政关系，在技术知识、资源需求和政治阻力方面都十分复杂且具有挑战性。例如，通过征收房产税来扩大地方财政收入，就会遭到城市居民的强烈抵制。

The third explanation is that Xi, a hardcore Leninist, saw the task of shoring up the foundations of Leninist rule as far more important and urgent than injecting a new dose of dynamism into the economy. Politically, he would also benefit from measures to strengthen party control over the state and society because these steps would centralize his authority and grant him more power. Not surprisingly, the institutional changes proposed in the decision gave Xi more direct control over national security, cybersecurity, and any major policy changes after he assumed his new roles as head of the new commissions and the "small leading groups" overseeing these domains.

第三种解释是，作为一名坚定的列宁主义者，习近平认为巩固列宁主义统治的基础远比为经济注入新的活力更为重要和紧迫。在政治上，加强党对国家和社会的控制也将使他受益，因为这些措施将集中他的权力，赋予他更大的权力。不出所料，该决定中提出的制度改革赋予了习近平在担任新委员会和负责这些领域的“小领导小组”组长后，对国家安全、网络安全以及任何重大政策变革更大的直接控制权。





Supply-Side Reform





供给侧改革


After abandoning his own package of economic reforms unveiled in November 2013, Xi opted for a set of more targeted measures at the end of 2015. Titled "supply-side reform," this program aims to address four major flaws in the Chinese economy: excess capacity, excess inventory, high debt leverage, and shortfalls in indigenous high-tech products. Conceived by his chief economic advisor, Vice Premier Liu He, supply-side reform was launched on November 10, 2015, and billed as an effort to increase the efficiency of the economy.15 Even though Xi appears to have invested enormous political capital in this package, including inserting supply-side reform into the CCP charter in late 2017, the reforms are more tactical than structural and do not confront the most serious economic problem: the imbalance between investment and consumption. Excess capacity and high debt levels, however serious, are symptoms, not causes, of the structural flaws in an economy in which the state controls too much capital and invests it wastefully. Additionally, these reforms were implemented almost exclusively through administrative fiat, thus resulting in discrimination against the private sector.

在放弃了2013年11月公布的经济改革方案后，习近平于2015年底选择了一系列更有针对性的措施。这项名为“供给侧改革”的计划旨在解决中国经济的四大弊病：产能过剩、库存过剩、高负债率和自主高科技产品短缺。供给侧改革由其首席经济顾问、国务院副总理刘鹤提出，于2015年11月10日正式启动，并被标榜为提高经济效率的举措。尽管习近平似乎为这一方案投入了大量政治资本，包括在2017年底将供给侧改革写入中共党章，但这些改革更多的是策略性的而非结构性的，并没有触及最严重的经济问题：投资与消费之间的不平衡。产能过剩和高负债水平固然严重，但它们只是国家控制过多资本并进行浪费性投资等结构性缺陷的症状，而非根源。此外，这些改革几乎完全是通过行政命令实施的，从而导致对私营部门的歧视。

Excess industrial capacity has been a chronic problem in China due to overinvestment by local governments seeking to expand their economic fiefdom. Local officials have additional political incentives to create large industrial firms under their control because they can then generate economic activities that will help improve their chances for promotion. Consequently, as most local government officials play this game, their decisions unavoidably lead to the construction of factories that supply more than the market demands, and the brutal price competition in sectors with excess production capacity leads to financial losses. Unlike in market economies where there are hard budget constraints (firms do not have unlimited access to funds), loss-making firms owned by local governments in China, free from such constraints, can count on the local authorities to fund their losses and keep them afloat. In the post-Mao era, industries producing consumer goods have become liberalized and dominated by private and foreign firms. Excess capacity in these industries is usually eliminated by the exit of uncompetitive firms. But because SOEs maintain a significant presence, or even dominance, in heavy industries, such as steel, nonferrous metals, cement, chemicals, and coal, SOE access to subsidies and bailouts makes it difficult to eliminate excess capacity.16

在中国，由于地方政府为扩张经济版图而过度投资，工业产能过剩一直是一个长期存在的问题。地方官员还有额外的政治动机去创建由其控制的大型工业企业，因为这些企业能够创造经济活动，从而提升自身的晋升机会。因此，由于大多数地方官员都参与了这种博弈，他们的决策不可避免地导致工厂产能过剩，而产能过剩行业残酷的价格竞争最终导致企业亏损。与市场经济中存在严格的预算约束（企业无法无限获取资金）不同，在中国，由地方政府拥有的亏损企业不受此类约束，可以依靠地方政府为其亏损买单，维持运营。后毛泽东时代，消费品生产行业逐渐走向自由化，并被私营企业和外资企业所主导。这些行业的产能过剩通常会通过不具竞争力的企业退出市场而得到消除。但由于国有企业在钢铁、有色金属、水泥、化工和煤炭等重工业领域保持着相当大的份额，甚至占据主导地位，因此国有企业能够获得补贴和救助，这使得消除过剩产能变得困难。

Xi's supply-side reform package set ambitious targets for reducing excess capacity in heavy industry. In the case of crude steel, the State Council announced in February 2016 that it was seeking to cut capacity by 100-150 million tons within five years (8-12 percent of total capacity).17 Subsequently, the government painted a rosy picture of the progress of the reform, claiming it had removed more than 140 million tons of steel industry capacity between 2016 and September 2018.18 But data from the National Bureau of Statistics show more modest progress. China's production capacity for crude steel was cut from 1.126 billion tons in 2015 to 1.085 billion tons in 2020. This means that, within five years, Xi's reform succeeded in cutting only 41 million tons of crude steel, much less than the target set in early 2016. Like steel, cement production capacity was reduced only marginally as well, from 3.442 billion tons to 3.397 billion tons (i.e., only 45 million tons, or 1.3 percent), during the same period.19

习近平的供给侧改革方案为削减重工业过剩产能设定了雄心勃勃的目标。以粗钢为例，国务院于2016年2月宣布，计划在五年内削减1亿至1.5亿吨产能（占总产能的8%至12%）。随后，政府对改革进展描绘了一幅乐观的图景，声称在2016年至2018年9月期间，钢铁行业已削减超过1.4亿吨产能。但国家统计局的数据显示，实际进展更为有限。中国粗钢产能从2015年的11.26亿吨削减至2020年的10.85亿吨。这意味着，在五年内，习近平的改革仅成功削减了4100万吨粗钢产能，远低于2016年初设定的目标。与钢铁类似，同期水泥产能的削减幅度也较小，从34.42亿吨降至33.97亿吨（即仅削减4500万吨，降幅1.3%）。

After the 2008 global financial crisis, China relied heavily on an expansion of the supply of credit through the financial system to sustain growth. Consequently, the level of debt in the nonfinancial sector grew rapidly. However, during the initial three years of Xi's first term, the party made no effort to slow down the borrowing. The average annual increase in credit to the nonfinancial sector was nearly 16 percent between 2013 and 2015, two percentage points more than that in 2009-2012, during which time credit growth had skyrocketed. By the end of 2015, credit to the nonfinancial sector stood at 239 percent of GDP, creating a potential financial crisis that would be a serious threat to the Chinese economy.20 One unique feature of China's high levels of debt further exacerbated the risks of a financial crisis: heavy borrowing by local governments (mostly through local government financing vehicles).

2008年全球金融危机后，中国严重依赖金融体系信贷供应扩张来维持经济增长。因此，非金融部门的债务水平迅速增长。然而，在习近平第一任期的头三年，中共并未采取任何措施来放缓借贷。2013年至2015年，非金融部门信贷年均增长率接近16%，比2009年至2012年信贷增长迅猛的时期高出两个百分点。到2015年底，非金融部门信贷占GDP的比重达到239%，这造成了潜在的金融危机，对中国经济构成严重威胁。中国高额债务的一个独特之处在于：地方政府（主要通过地方政府融资机构）的大量借贷，这进一步加剧了金融危机的风险。

The primary reason for the buildup of local debt was the 1994 fiscal reform that recentralized revenue without shifting expenditures from the localities to Beijing. In 1993, the year before fiscal recentralization, local governments received nearly 80 percent of total revenue. But after the reform, their share fell to about 50 percent. The share of public expenditures borne by local governments remained the same, however, at around 80 percent of all public expenditures. This created a huge structural deficit for local governments, equivalent to 30 percent of total public revenue. The structural shortfall of revenue means that local governments lacked funds to invest in infrastructure and other big-ticket items. Aside from seeking funding from Beijing, an unreliable solution, local governments grew increasingly dependent on revenues from land sales and borrowing to fund local infrastructure and, in the less wealthy areas, even to cover routine operational expenses.21

地方债务累积的主要原因是1994年的财政改革，该改革虽然实现了财政收入的集中化，但并未将支出从地方转移到北京。在财政集中化前一年，即1993年，地方政府获得了近80%的财政收入。但改革后，这一比例下降到约50%。然而，地方政府承担的公共支出比例保持不变，约为公共支出总额的80%。这造成了地方政府巨大的结构性赤字，相当于公共收入总额的30%。财政收入的结构性短缺意味着地方政府缺乏资金投资基础设施和其他大型项目。除了向北京寻求资金（但这并非可靠的解决方案）之外，地方政府越来越依赖土地出售和借贷收入来资助地方基础设施建设，在欠发达地区，甚至连日常运营开支也难以维持。

The magnitude of land-related revenues for local public finance can be seen in the following numbers. In 2020 land-related taxes, 2 trillion yuan, contributed roughly 20 percent of total local tax revenue. But proceeds from land sales were a whopping 8.4 trillion yuan, equivalent to 80 percent of total local tax revenue. Typically, local governments use the land under their control as collateral to borrow from the banks. This creates a huge risk because the land pledged as collateral is illiquid, and its value is difficult to determine. As the true value of the land critically depends on the real estate market, a deterioration of that market will impair the value of the collateral and inflict large losses on banks.22

以下数据足以说明土地相关收入对地方公共财政的重要性。2020年，土地相关税收为2万亿元人民币，约占地方税收总额的20%。但土地出让收入高达8.4万亿元人民币，相当于地方税收总额的80%。通常情况下，地方政府会将管辖土地作为抵押品向银行贷款。这会带来巨大的风险，因为作为抵押的土地流动性差，且其价值难以确定。由于土地的真实价值高度依赖于房地产市场，因此房地产市场的恶化将损害抵押品的价值，并给银行造成巨额损失。

As discussed earlier, local governments did not begin their borrowing binge until the Hu administration launched its credit-fueled stimulus package in 2008-2009. In subsequent years, the amount of debt owed by local governments exploded. Official data on local debt authorized by the central government report 15.4 trillion yuan at the end of 2014. However, local governments kept far more debt off the books. Estimates by economists suggest that the amount of off-the-books debt borrowed by local governments could have been 200-250 percent of the amount on the books. What this implies is that at the end of 2014, real local debt might have been 45-53 trillion yuan, or 70-82 percent of GDP. The deleveraging campaign does not appear to have lowered the leverage, as local governments reported total debt of 18.4 trillion yuan on their books at the end of 2018. Moreover, in subsequent years, local debt continued to grow. At the end of 2021, the officially declared amount of local debt was 30 trillion yuan, implying that real local debt might have been as high as 90-105 trillion yuan, or 80-93 percent of GDP.23

如前所述，地方政府的借贷狂潮始于胡锦涛政府在2008-2009年推出信贷驱动型刺激计划之后。此后几年，地方政府的债务规模呈爆炸式增长。官方数据显示，截至2014年底，中央批准的地方债务总额为15.4万亿元人民币。然而，地方政府账外债务远超账面数字。经济学家估计，地方政府账外借款额可能高达账面债务的200%-250%。这意味着，截至2014年底，地方实际债务可能达到45万亿至53万亿元人民币，占GDP的70%-82%。去杠杆化运动似乎并未降低杠杆率，截至2018年底，地方政府账面债务总额仍高达18.4万亿元人民币。此外，此后几年，地方债务持续增长。截至2021年底，官方公布的地方债务总额为30万亿元人民币，这意味着实际地方债务可能高达90万亿至105万亿元人民币，占GDP的80%至93%。

Of all the outstanding nonfinancial sector debt at the end of 2015, corporations, both state-owned and private, accounted for roughly two-thirds (about 108 trillion yuan), according to the Chinese central bank. Of this amount, roughly 40 percent was borrowed by local-government-owned SOEs (including many local government financing vehicles) that were typically smaller, less profitable, and more leveraged. Loans extended to SOEs in general, and to local SOEs in particular, are far riskier because these firms are less profitable than private firms. Perversely, due to their political influence and privileged positions in the economy, they also have greater access to credit, thus enabling them to borrow more.24

据中国央行统计，截至2015年底，所有未偿非金融部门债务中，国有和私营企业约占三分之二（约108万亿元人民币）。其中，约40%的债务由地方政府所有的国有企业（包括许多地方政府融资机构）借入，这些企业通常规模较小、盈利能力较低、杠杆率较高。由于国有企业的盈利能力低于私营企业，因此向国有企业（尤其是地方国有企业）提供的贷款风险更高。然而，由于其政治影响力和在经济中的特殊地位，这些企业也更容易获得信贷，从而能够借入更多资金。

Like other so-called reforms during the Xi era, deleveraging—reducing the debt-to-asset ratios—was implemented by administrative fiat. Banks were ordered to call in loans regardless of their credit risks. Because private firms with weak political connections could not shield themselves from this campaign, the main burdens fell on the private sector. When their lenders demanded early payment, many private firms that had pledged their assets as collateral were forced either to sell (mostly to SOEs) or to declare bankruptcy.25 Deleveraging also raised the borrowing costs for private firms due to the perception that they carried heightened credit risks.26 One piece of evidence suggesting that the private sector bore the brunt of the deleveraging campaign is that the outstanding amount of debt borrowed by nonfinancial SOEs actually rose by 10 trillion yuan in the first two years after the launch of the deleveraging campaign in 2016.27

与习近平时代其他所谓的改革一样，去杠杆化——降低资产负债率——是通过行政命令实施的。银行被要求催收贷款，无论其信用风险如何。由于政治关系薄弱的民营企业无法免受这场运动的影响，主要负担落在了私营部门身上。当贷款方要求提前还款时，许多以资产作抵押的民营企业被迫出售资产（大多卖给了国有企业）或宣布破产。去杠杆化也提高了民营企业的借贷成本，因为人们普遍认为它们的信用风险更高。一个证据表明，私营部门承受了去杠杆化运动的大部分冲击：2016年去杠杆化运动启动后的头两年，非金融国有企业的未偿债务总额实际上增加了10万亿元人民币。

The party abruptly halted the deleveraging campaign in mid-2018 after the start of the US-China trade war. Chinese leaders apparently worried that they could not risk slower growth in the middle of the worst trade conflict in the post-Cold War era. The phrase "deleveraging" suddenly disappeared from official rhetoric and was soon replaced by a new phrase—"stabilizing leverage."28

2018年中美贸易战爆发后，中共突然停止了去杠杆化运动。显然，中国领导人担心，在冷战后最严重的贸易冲突中，经济增长放缓的风险太大。“去杠杆化”一词突然从官方话语中消失，很快被“稳定杠杆”这一新词所取代。

Based on data from the Bank of International Settlements, China's debt level was rising, instead of declining, during the deleveraging campaign. At the end of 2015, credit to the nonfinancial sector stood at 239 percent of GDP. By the time Xi ended the campaign in July 2018, it was 260 percent of GDP. If we judge the success of deleveraging by the amount of the reduction in the growth of debt, then the deleveraging campaign can be considered a modest success because the debt grew at an annual rate of 8.4 percentage points of GDP during this period, compared with 15.6 percent during 2013-2015. In the four years after the official end of the deleveraging campaign, debt growth averaged 8.5 percentage points of GDP each year.29 The singular achievement of deleveraging was a reduction in the growth of debt, not a reduction in the leverage itself. In spite of the slower growth of debt, however, China's high leverage continued to threaten the stability of its financial sector and deprive its leaders of policy options when the economy was confronted with prospects of stagnant growth and deflation, as was the case in mid-2023.

根据国际清算银行的数据，在去杠杆化运动期间，中国的债务水平不降反升。2015年底，非金融部门信贷占GDP的239%。到2018年7月习近平结束去杠杆化运动时，这一比例已达260%。如果我们以债务增长速度的下降幅度来衡量去杠杆化的成功，那么去杠杆化运动只能算作一次小成功，因为在此期间，债务年均增长率仅为GDP的8.4个百分点，而2013-2015年期间的这一数字为15.6%。在去杠杆化运动正式结束后的四年里，债务年均增长率为GDP的8.5个百分点。去杠杆化的唯一成果是降低了债务增长速度，而非降低了杠杆率本身。尽管债务增长速度放缓，但中国的高杠杆率仍然威胁着其金融部门的稳定，并在经济面临增长停滞和通货紧缩的前景时（例如 2023 年年中），剥夺了其领导人的政策选择权。





The Housing Bubble





房地产泡沫


In 2003 the government designated the real estate sector as a "pillar industry." In the following decade, the explosive expansion of the sector turned it into one of the main drivers of growth. In 2003 investment in the sector was only 1 trillion yuan. By 2012, the end of the Hu period, investment in the sector reached 7.18 trillion yuan.30 During the Xi period, the growth of investment in the sector cooled off. In absolute terms, however, massive resources were nevertheless misallocated into the overbuilt sector. Cumulatively, between 2013 and 2023, real estate investment totaled 120 trillion yuan, almost equal to China's GDP in 2023 (table 7.1).

2003年，政府将房地产行业列为“支柱产业”。在接下来的十年里，该行业经历了爆炸式增长，成为经济增长的主要动力之一。2003年，房地产行业投资额仅为1万亿元人民币。到2012年胡锦涛时代末期，该行业投资额已达7.18万亿元人民币。习近平时代，该行业投资增速放缓。然而，从绝对值来看，大量资源仍然被错误地配置到过度建设的房地产领域。2013年至2023年，房地产投资累计达120万亿元人民币，几乎相当于2023年中国的GDP（表7.1）。

TABLE 7.1. Investment in Real Estate, 2013-2023

To make things worse, the booming sector led to a rapid increase in housing prices, prompting the government to take repeated measures to cool housing. Starting in 2005, the State Council issued a series of documents to control excess investment in the real estate sector and to restrict purchases so to dampen speculative behavior. These measures, however, had at best a marginal impact on containing the surging housing prices, especially in the largest and most prosperous cities, such as Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen.31

更糟糕的是，房地产行业的蓬勃发展导致房价迅速上涨，促使政府多次采取措施为房地产市场降温。自2005年起，国务院发布了一系列文件，旨在控制房地产行业的过度投资，限制购房，以抑制投机行为。然而，这些措施对遏制房价飙升的效果充其量也只是微乎其微，尤其是在上海、北京和深圳等规模最大、最繁荣的城市。

Several factors made it difficult for the government to prevent a housing bubble. First, at the national level, the housing sector contributed close to one-third of annual GDP growth by the end of the 2010s.32 Thus a drastic slowdown in the housing sector would hurt growth. Second, local governments depended on the housing sector for revenue. In addition to the taxes collected from real estate transactions, the income realized through the sale of land to developers and the credit obtained from banks using land as collateral constituted the principal sources of nontax revenue for local governments.

多种因素使得政府难以阻止房地产泡沫的出现。首先，在国家层面，到2010年代末，住房部门对年度GDP增长的贡献接近三分之一。因此，住房部门的急剧放缓将损害经济增长。其次，地方政府依赖住房部门的收入。除了房地产交易征收的税款外，通过向开发商出售土地获得的收入以及以土地为抵押从银行获得的信贷，构成了地方政府非税收入的主要来源。

Therefore, the local governments had incentives to sustain the real estate boom as long as possible. Third, housing—in particular, housing in large cities—was perhaps the only profitable asset for Chinese savers. Capital controls made it impossible to invest abroad, while the volatile domestic stock market, dominated by the inefficient SOEs, delivered poor results. As a result, the overlapping interests of a growth-obsessed central government, revenue-hungry local authorities, aggressive real estate developers, and residents seeking better housing or higher investment returns fueled the housing bubble and kept it from crashing.33

因此，地方政府有动机尽可能长时间地维持房地产繁荣。第三，住房——尤其是大城市的住房——或许是当时中国储户唯一有利可图的资产。资本管制使得海外投资变得不可能，而受低效国有企业主导、波动剧烈的国内股市表现不佳。结果，一心追求经济增长的中央政府、渴望财政收入的地方政府、积极进取的房地产开发商以及寻求更好住房或更高投资回报的居民之间利益的交织，助长了房地产泡沫，并使其免于破裂。

In December 2016 Xi Jinping personally ordered the first serious effort to cool the housing sector when he declared that "housing is for living, not for speculation." This mantra instantly prompted the government to adopt tough regulations. In addition to limiting the number of housing units individuals or families could purchase, the crackdown included prohibitions against selling new units within two years after the initial purchase, higher interest rates on mortgages, a ban on the issuance of mortgages to purchasers who already owned two units, and an increase in the supply of low-cost rental housing.34

2016年12月，习近平亲自下令，首次认真采取措施给房地产市场降温，他提出“住房是用来居住的，不是用来炒房的”。这一口号立即促使政府出台了一系列严格的监管措施。除了限制个人或家庭购房数量外，整顿措施还包括禁止在首次购房后两年内出售新房、提高抵押贷款利率、禁止向已拥有两套房产的购房者发放抵押贷款，以及增加低价租赁住房的供应。

Despite implementation of these measures, the bubble in the housing sector grew bigger, albeit at a slower pace. The amount of investment in the real estate sector rose on average 8.4 percent per year between 2017 and 2019, 50 percent more than the annual average growth of 5.7 percent between 2014 and 2016, but nearly a third of the annual average increase in growth of 22.6 percent recorded between 2009 and 2013.35 Instead of declining, the average price per square meter rose, from slightly under 7,500 yuan to 10,000 yuan, from 2016 to 2020.36

尽管采取了这些措施，房地产泡沫仍然扩大，尽管增速放缓。2017年至2019年间，房地产投资额年均增长8.4%，比2014年至2016年间5.7%的年均增速高出50%，但仅为2009年至2013年间22.6%年均增速的三分之一左右。此外，平均每平方米价格不降反升，从2016年的略低于7500元人民币涨至2020年的10000元人民币。

The ineffectiveness of the policies implemented after Xi's edict forced the government to double down in 2020, despite the economic downturn attributed to the Covid-19 pandemic. In August the government rolled out an unprecedented regulation, popularly known as the "three red lines," to force developers to reduce their leverage. Specifically, developers could increase their debt level by 15 percent if they met three criteria: a liability-to-asset ratio of less than 70 percent (excluding prepayments made by purchasers for unfinished housing units), net debt below total equity, and cash on hand equal to or exceeding 100 percent of short-term debt. If they met only two of the three criteria, they could increase their leverage by 10 percent. If they met only one of the three, they could raise their debt level by 5 percent. If they failed on all three measures, they could not raise their debt level. The government likely intended for this seemingly nuanced policy to achieve a soft landing in the housing bubble. However, the government did not anticipate the risks of contagion precipitated by the loss of access to credit by even a small number of highly indebted real estate developers. At the time of the policy announcement, about one-quarter of China's two hundred largest real estate firms met none of the three criteria and were facing the prospect of losing access to credit. Consequently, implementation of the policy precipitated a disorderly unwinding of China's real estate bubble that could not have been the original intention of policymakers.37

尽管新冠疫情导致经济下滑，但习近平指示后实施的政策效果不佳，迫使政府在2020年加大力度。8月，政府推出了一项前所未有的规定，即俗称的“三条红线”，旨在强制开发商降低杠杆率。具体而言，如果开发商满足以下三个条件，则可以提高15%的负债水平：负债资产比率低于70%（不包括购房者预付的未完工房屋款项）、净负债低于总权益、以及现金储备等于或超过短期债务的100%。如果仅满足三个条件中的两个，则可以提高10%的杠杆率。如果仅满足其中一个，则可以提高5%的杠杆率。如果三个条件均不满足，则无法提高杠杆率。政府很可能希望通过这项看似微妙的政策，实现房地产泡沫的软着陆。然而，政府并未预料到，即使只有少数负债累累的房地产开发商失去信贷渠道，也会引发连锁反应的风险。政策出台之时，中国两百家最大的房地产企业中，约有四分之一不符合上述三项标准中的任何一项，面临失去信贷渠道的风险。因此，该政策的实施导致了中国房地产泡沫的无序破裂，这显然并非政策制定者的初衷。

Unlike previous attempts, the "three red lines" perhaps worked too well, judging by the implosion of the real estate sector that was to follow. In 2021 investment in the sector grew only 4.3 percent, and sales measured in floor space rose only 1.9 percent. Ominously, the amount of land purchased by developers for potential projects, a leading indicator, fell 15.5 percent.38 For the heavily indebted real estate developers, enforcement of the three red lines sounded a death knell. Evergrande, one of China's largest real estate developers that met none of the three criteria, was immediately pushed to the brink of insolvency. Saddled with nearly two trillion yuan of debt, Evergrande could not raise new debt to pay its bills. By August 2023, it filed for bankruptcy and its founder was placed under criminal investigation.39 The unavoidable contagion triggered by Evergrande's default quickly plunged other large and equally indebted real estate developers into a liquidity crisis after they lost access to new financing.

与以往的尝试不同，从随后房地产行业的崩盘来看，“三条红线”或许效果过头了。2021年，该行业的投资仅增长4.3%，以建筑面积衡量的销售额仅增长1.9%。更令人担忧的是，作为领先指标的开发商为潜在项目购置的土地数量下降了15.5%。对于负债累累的房地产开发商而言，“三条红线”的实施无异于敲响了丧钟。恒大是中国最大的房地产开发商之一，由于不符合这三条标准中的任何一条，立即被推到了破产的边缘。背负着近两万亿元人民币债务的恒大，根本无力筹集新的资金来偿还债务。到 2023 年 8 月，恒大申请破产，其创始人被刑事调查。恒大违约引发的不可避免的连锁反应，迅速使其他规模庞大且负债累累的房地产开发商陷入流动性危机，因为它们失去了获得新融资的渠道。

The deflation of the real estate bubble accelerated in 2022 when investment in the sector fell 10 percent from the previous year. Sales measured by transactions dropped 27 percent.40 In 2023 the real estate sector was in a meltdown. By September, two-thirds of the top fifty private real estate firms were in default of their dollar-denominated bonds.41 Housing prices in major cities recorded a consistent decline despite the government's efforts to limit the fall in sale prices and the use of massaged data to conceal the extent of the decline in prices.42 Compared with 2022, sales of homes by floor space fell 7.5 percent in the first nine months of 2023, while investment in the real estate sector declined by 9.5 percent for the whole year.43

2022年，房地产泡沫的破裂加速，该行业的投资额较上年下降10%，交易量下降27%。2023年，房地产行业陷入崩溃。到9月份，排名前50位的私营房地产公司中，有三分之二的美元债券违约。尽管政府努力限制房价下跌，并利用数据操纵掩盖价格下跌的程度，但主要城市的房价仍持续下降。与2022年相比，2023年前九个月，按建筑面积计算的房屋销售量下降了7.5%，而全年房地产行业的投资额下降了9.5%。

The crash of the real estate sector in 2023-2024 dragged down the economy and forced the government to relax enforcement of the three red lines. To resuscitate the real estate sector, local governments scrapped the restrictions on purchasing homes, and banking regulators lowered the amount of down payment required to obtain mortgages.44 However, the crisis in the real estate sector was so vast and deep that these modest measures did not make much of a difference. The housing sector is expected to be weak and to depress growth for years to come.45

2023-2024年房地产市场的崩盘拖累了整体经济，迫使政府放松了“三红线”的执行力度。为了重振房地产市场，地方政府取消了购房限制，银行监管机构也降低了抵押贷款的首付比例。然而，房地产市场的危机规模巨大且影响深远，这些小幅措施收效甚微。预计未来几年住房市场将持续疲软，并抑制经济增长。





The US-China Trade War





美中贸易战


Sino-American trade tensions were simmering even before the trade war launched by Donald Trump in 2018. After China joined the WTO in December 2001, bilateral merchandise trade boomed. In 2001 the United States exported $19 billion worth of goods to China and imported $102 billion. By the time Trump won his surprise victory in 2016, the United States was exporting $116 billion to China and importing $462 billion from China.46 During this period, a persistent high trade deficit, restricted market access in China, and violations of the intellectual property rights of US firms stoked tensions between Washington and Beijing. However, the high-level exchanges between China and the United States on trade yielded no meaningful outcomes. America's trade deficit with China remained stubbornly high, while charges of theft of intellectual property and of China's failure to honor its WTO commitments grew louder.

中美贸易紧张局势早在2018年唐纳德·特朗普发起贸易战之前就已暗流涌动。自中国于2001年12月加入世贸组织以来，双边商品贸易蓬勃发展。2001年，美国对华出口额为190亿美元，进口额为1020亿美元。到2016年特朗普意外胜选时，美国对华出口额已达1160亿美元，从中国进口额高达4620亿美元。在此期间，持续高企的贸易逆差、中国市场准入受限以及美国企业知识产权遭到侵犯等问题，加剧了华盛顿和北京之间的紧张关系。然而，中美之间就贸易问题进行的高层磋商并未取得任何实质性成果。美国对华贸易逆差居高不下，而美国对中国窃取知识产权和违反世贸组织承诺的指责也愈演愈烈。

Disappointment over China's lack of action to address these concerns eroded corporate America's goodwill. Even more important, the combination of technological change and globalization resulted in the loss of millions of blue-collar manufacturing jobs in America's politically crucial rust belt, creating an opening for a populist like Trump to exploit resentment among these victims of globalization. During his presidential bid in 2016, Trump adroitly seized the trade issue, accusing China of "raping" America and engaging in the "greatest theft in the history of the world."47

由于中国未能采取行动解决这些问题，美国企业界的失望情绪日益加剧，其好感度也随之下降。更重要的是，技术变革和全球化的结合导致美国政治重镇“铁锈地带”数百万蓝领制造业岗位流失，这为像特朗普这样的民粹主义者提供了可乘之机，使其得以利用这些全球化受害者的不满情绪。在2016年总统竞选期间，特朗普巧妙地抓住了贸易问题，指责中国“掠夺”美国，并犯下了“世界历史上最大的盗窃罪”。

After he entered the White House, Trump appointed a trade hawk, Robert Lighthizer, as his trade representative. In August 2017 Lighthizer initiated an investigation into China's violations of America's intellectual property rights. In early April of the following year, he produced a report finding China in violation of intellectual property rights. As a penalty, the report proposed levying 25 percent additional tariffs on $50 billion of Chinese goods imported into the United States. China reacted by threatening to impose 25 percent tariffs on $50 billion of American goods exported to China. Thus began the largest trade war in post-World War II history to that time.

特朗普入主白宫后，任命贸易鹰派人物罗伯特·莱特希泽担任贸易代表。2017年8月，莱特希泽启动了对中国侵犯美国知识产权的调查。次年4月初，他发布报告，认定中国侵犯了美国的知识产权。作为惩罚措施，该报告提议对价值500亿美元的中国输美商品加征25%的关税。中国随即威胁对价值500亿美元的美国输华商品加征25%的关税。由此，二战后规模最大的贸易战拉开了序幕。

As Xi responded to Trump's trade war with retaliatory tariffs on American goods, the United States and China engaged in a series of negotiations in an attempt to resolve their disputes, albeit without much success. A ray of hope for an ending to the trade war emerged in early 2019 when it appeared that China might accept an American proposal that would force major changes in its trading practices. But the CCP Politburo Standing Committee rejected the proposal, a development that prompted an infuriated Trump to escalate the trade war.48 Subsequently, Trump extended tariffs of between 10 and 25 percent on nearly all Chinese imports to the United States. But in January 2020 the two countries signed the so-called Phase One Deal that withheld planned further tariff increases on $160 billion worth of Chinese imports, cut tariffs from 15 to 7.5 percent on $120 billion of Chinese goods, but maintained the 25 percent tariff on $250 billion worth of Chinese imports. In return, China pledged to increase its purchases of American exports and services by at least $200 billion over the next two years. Although Trump touted the deal as a “win,” China did not buy the promised extra American goods and services in 2020 and 2021.49

在习近平以对美国商品加征报复性关税回应特朗普的贸易战后，中美两国展开了一系列谈判，试图解决争端，但收效甚微。2019年初，贸易战似乎出现了一线曙光：中国似乎可能接受美国的一项提议，该提议将迫使中国对其贸易做法进行重大调整。然而，中共中央政治局常委会否决了这项提议，这激怒了特朗普，导致贸易战升级。随后，特朗普对几乎所有中国输美商品加征了10%至25%的关税。但在2020年1月，两国签署了所谓的“第一阶段协议”，该协议暂停了对价值1600亿美元的中国进口商品进一步加征关税的计划，并将价值1200亿美元的中国商品的关税从15%降至7.5%，但维持了对价值2500亿美元的中国进口商品25%的关税。作为交换，中国承诺在未来两年内至少增加2000亿美元的美国出口商品和服务采购。尽管特朗普称该协议为“胜利”，但中国在2020年和2021年并未购买承诺的额外美国商品和服务。

By the time Trump left office in January 2021, the trade war had placed additional cumulative tariffs on $550 billion of Chinese imports, while China had retaliated with cumulative punitive tariffs on $185 billion worth of American products. After Joe Biden entered the White House, he kept Trump's tariffs in place, both because reducing or removing them would cost him dearly in a country in which protrade policies were no longer popular and because the ongoing deterioration in US-China relations made such a concession difficult.50

到特朗普于2021年1月卸任时，贸易战已对价值5500亿美元的中国进口商品加征了累计关税，而中国也对价值1850亿美元的美国商品加征了累计惩罚性关税作为报复。乔·拜登入主白宫后，维持了特朗普的关税政策，原因有二：一是在美国，减少或取消这些关税会让他付出沉重代价，因为美国的贸易友好政策已不再受欢迎；二是美中关系的持续恶化使得做出这样的让步变得困难重重。

Despite the ferocity of the trade war, its immediate economic impact was modest. China's GDP growth was 7.3 percent in 2017; it fell to 6.4 percent in 2018 and to 6.1 percent in 2019.51 US GDP growth rose from 2.2 in 2017 to 2.9 percent in 2018, but it fell to 2.2 percent in 2019.52 Most of the costs of the trade war—higher prices of China-made consumer goods due to the additional tariffs—were borne by American consumers.53

尽管贸易战激烈，但其直接的经济影响并不显著。2017年中国GDP增长率为7.3%，2018年降至6.4%，2019年进一步降至6.1%。美国GDP增长率从2017年的2.2%上升至2018年的2.9%，但2019年降至2.2%。贸易战的大部分成本——由于加征关税导致中国制造的消费品价格上涨——最终由美国消费者承担。

Judging by trade and investment flows, the trade war appears to have had only a minor impact on China. To be sure, China's exports to the United States in 2018 and 2019 fell significantly as the result of higher tariffs (table 7.2). The Covid-19 pandemic, which caused disruptions, further depressed Chinese exports to the United States in 2020. But in 2021 and 2022, Chinese exports to the United States recovered to the level prior to the trade war. The effects of "decoupling" became more pronounced starting in 2023, when Chinese exports to the United States fell to $427 billion, a decline of 20 percent from 2022.

从贸易和投资流动来看，贸易战对中国的影响似乎并不显著。诚然，由于关税上调，中国2018年和2019年对美出口大幅下降（见表7.2）。新冠疫情造成的经济中断进一步抑制了2020年中国对美出口。但到了2021年和2022年，中国对美出口已恢复到贸易战前的水平。“脱钩”的影响从2023年开始变得更加明显，当年中国对美出口降至4270亿美元，较2022年下降了20%。

China's overall foreign trade was not initially affected by the trade war. Exports grew moderately between 2018 and 2020 and exploded between 2021 and 2022, likely reflecting China's central role in the global supply chains. Overall trade in 2023 held steady if measured in RMB but declined 5 percent in dollar terms, reflecting the depreciation of the Chinese currency (table 7.3)

中国整体对外贸易最初并未受到贸易战的影响。2018年至2020年间，出口温和增长，2021年至2022年间则出现爆发式增长，这可能反映了中国在全球供应链中的核心地位。2023年，以人民币计价的整体贸易额保持稳定，但以美元计价则下降了5%，这反映了人民币贬值（表7.3）。

In the immediate aftermath, foreign direct investment in China was more negatively affected by the trade war. In 2017 China recorded $181 billion in FDI. This amount fell to $135 billion in 2018 and $138 billion in 2019. It recovered close to the pre-trade-war level in 2021 ($173 billion) and 2022 ($189 billion).54

贸易战爆发后，对华外国直接投资的负面影响尤为显著。2017年，中国吸引外国直接投资1810亿美元。2018年和2019年，这一数字分别下降至1350亿美元和1380亿美元。2021年和2022年，中国外国直接投资逐渐恢复至接近贸易战前的水平，分别为1730亿美元和1890亿美元。

Despite the modest negative impact of the trade war on the Chinese economy in the short term, the US-China trade war marked the beginning of a "decoupling" of the Chinese economy from that of the United States and, to a lesser extent, from the economies of America's allies. On its own, the trade war raised the costs of Chinese goods in the United States, thus incentivizing manufacturers to relocate their manufacturing facilities to other countries, particularly to facilities in Southeast Asia, to avoid the additional tariffs. However, the trade war was not the sole trigger of the decoupling between the two economies. The outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 added another reason for the West to reduce its reliance on China. The pandemic inflicted massive disruptions on the global supply chains concentrated in China.55 For companies accustomed to counting on dependable deliveries from China, the disruptions caused by the lockdowns threatened normal operations.

尽管贸易战短期内对中国经济的负面影响不大，但中美贸易战标志着中国经济与美国经济（以及在较小程度上与美国盟友经济）“脱钩”的开始。贸易战本身推高了中国商品在美国的成本，从而促使制造商将生产设施转移到其他国家，特别是东南亚地区，以规避额外的关税。然而，贸易战并非两国经济脱钩的唯一导火索。2020年新冠疫情的爆发，为西方减少对中国的依赖增添了又一个理由。疫情对集中在中国的全球供应链造成了巨大冲击。对于那些习惯于依赖中国可靠供货的企业而言，封锁措施造成的干扰威胁到了其正常的运营。

Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 probably provided the most powerful incentive for Western manufacturers to accelerate relocation of their supply chains from China. After the war began, the West imposed unprecedented economic sanctions on Russia, freezing its assets and choking its access to Western imports and financial systems. In retaliation, Russia seized the assets of Western companies in Russia. The geopolitical risks of doing business with China rose exponentially overnight, mainly because of the prospect of a war between mainland China and Taiwan, which Beijing considers a breakaway province (in 1949, the defeated Chinese Nationalists withdrew to Taiwan, then part of China). A war across the Taiwan Strait would likely be far more economically devastating if the United States were to intervene to defend Taiwan. As China is the world's largest manufacturing economy and is far more integrated with the global economy than is Russia, fears of a catastrophic war involving mainland China, Taiwan, and potentially the United States immediately became an irresistible motivator for companies to move out of China or to source supplies from other countries.

2022年2月俄罗斯入侵乌克兰，或许是促使西方制造商加速将供应链从中国转移的最有力动力。战争爆发后，西方对俄罗斯实施了前所未有的经济制裁，冻结其资产，并切断其获取西方进口商品和金融体系的渠道。作为报复，俄罗斯查封了西方公司在俄罗斯的资产。与中国开展业务的地缘政治风险一夜之间呈指数级增长，这主要是因为中国大陆与台湾之间爆发战争的可能性。北京将台湾视为其分离省份（1949年，战败的国民党军队退守台湾，当时台湾是中国的一部分）。如果美国介入保卫台湾，台海战争造成的经济损失可能会更大。由于中国是世界最大的制造业经济体，并且与全球经济的融合程度远高于俄罗斯，因此，对中国大陆、台湾乃至美国之间可能爆发的灾难性战争的担忧，立即成为企业迁出中国或从其他国家采购原材料的强大动力。

To make matters worse, US-China relations continued to spiral downward after Joe Biden entered the White House. Even though on the surface Biden's strategy of containment did not advocate full-fledged economic decoupling, in practice the widespread perception in the business community that geopolitical tensions between the two countries were here to stay and could escalate out of control led to a repricing of the risks of doing business with or in China. Relations between Beijing and Brussels also fell victim to Russia's war against Ukraine. The Chinese-EU relationship had faced severe strains due to clashes over trade and human rights even before the war. Nevertheless, in the realm of security, China was eager to ensure the strategic neutrality of the EU in the Sino-American rivalry, and the EU was initially reluctant to take sides.

更糟糕的是，拜登入主白宫后，美中关系持续恶化。尽管拜登的遏制战略表面上并未主张彻底的经济脱钩，但实际上，商界普遍认为两国之间的地缘政治紧张局势将长期存在并可能失控升级，这导致企业重新评估了与中国开展业务或在华开展业务的风险。北京与布鲁塞尔的关系也因俄罗斯入侵乌克兰而受到影响。早在战争爆发前，中欧关系就因贸易和人权问题上的冲突而面临严峻考验。然而，在安全领域，中国渴望确保欧盟在中美竞争中保持战略中立，而欧盟最初也不愿选边站队。

When Vladimir Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine, less than three weeks after he signed a joint declaration with Xi announcing a “no-limit friendship,” the EU’s relationship with China took a fateful turn. The largest and most violent war in Europe since World War II rendered the EU’s efforts to maintain strategic neutrality in the Sino-American rivalry untenable. In the meantime, Washington’s unflinching support for Ukraine in resisting Russian aggression revealed to the EU not only its dependence on American power but also the value of an alliance with the United States that no amount of trade with China could match. Consequently, the EU took initial steps to reduce its economic ties with China. Some of its member states adopted investment restrictions and export controls targeting China even though the EU leadership preferred a less jarring phrase, “derisking,” as label for its policy.56

在弗拉基米尔·普京与习近平签署联合声明，宣布建立“无限友谊”不到三周后，普京下令入侵乌克兰，欧盟与中国的关系由此发生了重大转变。这场二战以来欧洲规模最大、伤亡最惨重的战争，使得欧盟在中美竞争中维持战略中立的努力难以为继。与此同时，华盛顿坚定不移地支持乌克兰抵抗俄罗斯的侵略，这不仅让欧盟意识到自身对美国实力的依赖，也让欧盟认识到与美国结盟的价值远非与中国的贸易所能比拟。因此，欧盟开始采取措施，逐步减少与中国的经济联系。尽管欧盟领导层更倾向于使用“降低风险”这一较为温和的措辞来描述其政策，但一些成员国还是对中国实施了投资限制和出口管制。

Trade and investment data for 2023 may offer a glimpse into the trend of decoupling between China and the West. Although several factors, such as rising interest rates in the United States, the resultant economic weaknesses in the West, and China's disappointing economic growth and historically high exports in 2022, likely muddy the picture in 2023, the amount of utilized FDI in 2023 was $163.2 billion, $13.9 billion less than the previous year. While overall exports held steady in 2023, Chinese exports to the United States fell far more dramatically. Between January and September 2023, China exported about $90 billion less goods to the United States than it did in the previous year, indicating an acceleration of the bilateral "decoupling."57 In all likelihood, the full negative effects of the trade war on China's exports and inbound FDI will play out over an extended period. As Trump launches another trade war following his return to the White House in 2025, Chinese exports could suffer another devastating blow.

2023年的贸易和投资数据或许能让我们一窥中西方脱钩的趋势。尽管美国利率上升、由此导致的西方经济疲软以及中国2022年令人失望的经济增长和历史性的高出口等诸多因素可能会使2023年的情况变得复杂，但2023年实际利用的外国直接投资额为1632亿美元，比上年减少了139亿美元。虽然2023年整体出口保持稳定，但中国对美国的出口降幅却更为显著。2023年1月至9月，中国对美国的商品出口额比上年同期减少了约900亿美元，这表明双边“脱钩”正在加速。贸易战对中国出口和外国直接投资的负面影响很可能需要一段时间才能完全显现。如果特朗普在 2025 年重返白宫后再次发动贸易战，中国出口可能会遭受又一次毁灭性打击。

The short-term negative impact of the US-China trade war on the Chinese economy might be moderate, as shown by trade and investment data. But the prospect of an economic "decoupling" between the United States and China has led to the most profound change in economic policy and orientation since the post-Mao era. When Deng launched reform and opening in 1979, integration with the capitalist economies in the West, most critically the development of trade and investment ties with the United States, the world's largest and technologically most advanced economy, was a strategic priority. In the four decades that followed Deng's January 1979 historic visit to Washington, China's impressive growth record was made possible, in large part, by its broad and dense economic ties with the West, in particular the United States.

贸易和投资数据显示，中美贸易战对中国经济的短期负面影响可能较为温和。但中美经济“脱钩”的前景，已导致中国经济政策和方向发生自后毛泽东时代以来最深刻的转变。1979年邓小平启动改革开放时，与西方资本主义经济体，特别是与世界最大、技术最先进的经济体——美国——发展贸易和投资关系，是中国的一项战略重点。在邓小平1979年1月历史性访美后的四十年间，中国令人瞩目的经济增长在很大程度上得益于其与西方，特别是与美国广泛而紧密的经济联系。

The free fall of Sino-American relations in the aftermath of the trade war threatened the viability of China's development strategy that focused on economic integration with the West. By early 2020, US-China decoupling was moving ahead at full steam, threatening not only hundreds of billions of dollars in bilateral merchandise trade but also Chinese access to advanced American technologies. During the first trade war, the Trump administration simultaneously began to impose a series of sanctions on Chinese technology companies by banning them from purchasing high-end semiconductors made in the United States or made with American technologies. Following the escalation of the trade war in May 2019, the United States put China's telecom giant Huawei, a global leader in 5G technology, on the so-called Entity List, thereby requiring that American firms planning to supply Huawei must first obtain a license from the Commerce Department, with the presumption that such applications would be denied.58

贸易战后中美关系急剧恶化，威胁到中国以与西方经济一体化为核心的发展战略的可行性。到2020年初，中美脱钩进程加速，不仅威胁到数千亿美元的双边商品贸易，也威胁到中国获取美国先进技术的途径。在第一次贸易战期间，特朗普政府同时开始对中国科技公司实施一系列制裁，禁止它们购买美国制造或采用美国技术制造的高端半导体。2019年5月贸易战升级后，美国将中国电信巨头华为（5G技术领域的全球领导者）列入所谓的“实体清单”，要求计划向华为供货的美国公司必须首先获得美国商务部的许可，而此类申请很可能被拒绝。

By spring 2020, the bottom of US-China relations fell out as Trump, increasingly worried about the damage of the raging Covid-19 pandemic on his reelection bid, gave the hawks in his administration carte blanche to punish China, the source of the virus. The collapsing US-China relations in general, and the decoupling between the two countries in particular, prompted Chinese leaders to draft a new economic strategy for a changed world.

到2020年春季，美中关系跌至谷底。特朗普日益担忧新冠疫情对其连任竞选造成不利影响，于是放任政府中的鹰派肆意惩罚病毒源头——中国。美中关系的全面崩溃，尤其是两国经济的脱钩，促使中国领导人制定新的经济战略以适应不断变化的世界格局。

In May 2020 Xi articulated the "dual circulation" strategy, a central concept in China's development approach for a world of great power rivalry and economic fragmentation. According to official media, the strategy of dual circulation was first proposed at a meeting of the Politburo Standing Committee on May 13, 2020. Shortly thereafter, Xi began to personally promote this idea in his public speeches. The Politburo formally endorsed the concept at the end of July 2020.59

2020年5月，习近平提出了“双循环”战略，这是中国在大国竞争和经济碎片化的世界格局下发展战略的核心概念。据官方媒体报道，“双循环”战略最早于2020年5月13日在中共中央政治局常委会会议上提出。此后不久，习近平开始在公开讲话中亲自宣传这一理念。2020年7月底，中共中央政治局正式通过了这一战略。

The concept of dual circulation was translated into policy in November 2020, when the Fifth Plenum of the Central Committee approved the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan and proposed the development goals for 2021-2035. The "Proposal of the CCP Central Committee on Formulating the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development and the Long-Term Goals for 2035" explicitly puts forth a new development strategy centered on domestic demand and technological self-reliance.60

双循环理念于2020年11月转化为政策，当时中共中央五中全会批准了“十四五”规划，并提出了2021—2035年的发展目标。《中共中央关于制定国民经济和社会发展“十四五”规划和2035年远期目标的建议》明确提出了以内需和技术自力更生为核心的新发展战略。

Based on authoritative statements by Xi himself as well as by his chief economic adviser, Vice Premier Liu He, the party's new development strategy was crafted in response to America's policy of containing China's rise through economic decoupling and the tech war. In his speech to the Fifth Plenum, Xi warned: "In recent years, along with the changes in the global political and economic environment, the upsurge in deglobalization and the unilateralism and protectionism acts by certain countries, the traditional global circulation has been notably weakened." He went on to urge that efforts be made "to root China's development inside the country and rely more on the domestic market to achieve economic growth."61

根据习近平本人及其首席经济顾问、国务院副总理刘鹤的权威表态，中共的新发展战略是为了应对美国通过经济脱钩和科技战遏制中国崛起的政策而制定的。习近平在五中全会讲话中警告说：“近年来，随着全球政治经济环境的变化、去全球化的抬头以及某些国家单边主义和保护主义行径的抬头，传统的全球循环明显减弱。”他进一步强调，要“让中国的发展扎根国内，更多地依靠国内市场实现经济增长”。

Both Xi and Liu offered upbeat assessments of the feasibility of dual circulation by listing China's size advantage: a middle-income country with 1.4 billion people and a market with the largest growth potential in the world. This huge market will be able to generate sufficient domestic demand to sustain growth in the future in spite of an unfriendly external environment because consumption will rise and producers will increase efficiency through the adoption of modern technology and improvements in supply chains.62

习近平和刘晓明都对双循环的可行性给予了乐观的评估，他们列举了中国的规模优势：中国是一个拥有14亿人口的中等收入国家，也是一个拥有全球最大增长潜力的市场。尽管外部环境不利，但这个庞大的市场仍能产生足够的内需，从而在未来维持经济增长，因为消费将会增长，生产者将通过采用现代技术和改进供应链来提高效率。

As a framework document, the proposal lists key objectives. The section on generating new sources of domestic demand refers to upgrading and increasing household consumption and providing more social services. However, the document does not include new policies that might actually raise household income to increase or upgrade consumption. Investment would retain its role as a key driver of growth as the proposal offers a long list of major infrastructure projects to be built in the coming years.

作为一份框架性文件，该提案列出了关键目标。关于创造新的国内需求来源的部分提到了提升和增加家庭消费以及提供更多社会服务。然而，该文件并未包含任何可能真正提高家庭收入以促进或提升消费的新政策。投资仍将是经济增长的关键驱动力，因为该提案列出了未来几年将要建设的一系列重大基础设施项目。

In addition to reducing reliance on external demand, the proposal also calls for greater resilience and security of supply chains and technological self-sufficiency. Reflecting his awareness of China's vulnerability to Western technological sanctions, Xi set the goal of resilience of supply chains in April 2020 when he addressed the Central Finance Small Group, the party's top economic decision-making body. He urged, "In order to ensure our industrial security and national security, we must strive to build self-reliant, controllable, secure, and dependable production and supply chains. We must seek to have at least one alternative source for critical products and supplies." In a veiled but obvious reference to a potential conflict with the United States, Xi stated that he believed that more resilient and secure supply chains centered domestically would help China increase its national security and allow it to "maintain normal economic activities under extreme conditions."63

除了减少对外部需求的依赖外，该提案还呼吁增强供应链的韧性和安全性，并实现技术自主。习近平意识到中国易受西方技术制裁的影响，于2020年4月在中央财政小组会议上提出增强供应链韧性的目标。中央财政小组是中共最高经济决策机构。他强调：“为了保障产业安全和国家安全，我们必须努力构建自力更生、可控、安全可靠的生产供应链。关键产品和物资至少要有一个备选来源。” 习近平在讲话中隐晦地提及了与美国可能发生的冲突，他表示，他相信以国内为中心、更具韧性和安全的供应链将有助于中国增强国家安全，并使中国能够在极端条件下“维持正常的经济活动”。

The proposals of the Fifth Plenum add more details to Xi's concept of economic security. Judging by the space devoted to technological self-sufficiency, it is evident that the party views this as an overriding priority. Section III of the proposals contain specific ambitious programs designed to enable China to develop indigenous capabilities and overcome the West's technological containment. These include formulation of a comprehensive plan that would mobilize the resources of the entire nation to achieve new scientific and technological progress, in particular in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing, semiconductors, and life sciences. Also mentioned are new large national research projects, talent recruitment programs, and incentives for innovation by domestic entities.64

五中全会的提案进一步细化了习近平提出的经济安全理念。从提案中对技术自给自足的篇幅来看，显然中共将其视为重中之重。提案第三部分包含一系列雄心勃勃的具体计划，旨在使中国能够发展自主能力，突破西方的技术封锁。这些计划包括制定一项综合规划，调动全国资源，在人工智能、量子计算、半导体和生命科学等新兴领域取得新的科技进步。此外，提案还提及了新的大型国家科研项目、人才引进计划以及对国内企业创新的激励措施。

Even though Xi tried to strike a balance between development and security, his speech to the plenum implies that security should override development. According to Xi, it will be wise to "overestimate difficulties [and] deepen our thinking about risks," implying that in devising a development strategy, China must give more weight to potential security risks.65 The proposal duly reflects Xi's broadened definition of security risks by declaring that China "must maintain its ability to secure and control critical industries, infrastructure, strategic resources, and major scientific and technological areas."66

尽管习近平试图在发展与安全之间取得平衡，但他在全会上的讲话暗示安全应优先于发展。习近平指出，要“高估困难，深化风险思考”，这意味着中国在制定发展战略时必须更加重视潜在的安全风险。该提议也体现了习近平对安全风险的更广泛定义，他宣称中国“必须保持对关键产业、基础设施、战略资源和重大科技领域的安全和管控能力”。

On the surface, Xi's vision of dual circulation does not entail severing ties with the global economy. But it is clear that dual circulation would consist primarily of "great domestic circulation" based on reliable domestic demand and secure sources of technology.67 In the years following issuance of this landmark document, the party implemented several measures to turn Xi's vision into reality. The bulk of efforts in 2021-2023 were on building a domestic semiconductor supply chain to overcome US-led efforts to cut off China's access to advanced chips.

表面上看，习近平提出的“双循环”构想并不意味着切断与全球经济的联系。但显然，“双循环”主要由以可靠的国内需求和可靠的技术来源为基础的“大国内循环”构成。在这一里程碑式文件发布后的几年里，中共实施了多项措施，将习近平的构想变为现实。2021年至2023年期间，重点工作是构建国内半导体供应链，以应对美国主导的切断中国获取先进芯片的企图。

In September 2023 China launched a new $40 billion state-backed fund to invest in the semiconductor industry. This was on top of the nearly $48 billion the government had raised between 2014 and 2019 for the China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund (ICF), commonly known as the "Big Fund."68 Although establishment of the Big Fund in 2014 long preceded the US-China tech war, Beijing's additional investment in September 2023 was definitely a direct response to America's escalating export controls to cripple China's semiconductor sector, in particular the package of measures the Biden administration unveiled in October 2022 that sought to block Chinese access to high-end chips and the equipment capable of producing them.

2023年9月，中国启动了一项规模达400亿美元的国家支持基金，用于投资半导体产业。此前，中国政府已在2014年至2019年间为中国集成电路产业投资基金（简称“大基金”）筹集了近480亿美元。尽管大基金的设立远早于中美科技战，但北京在2023年9月追加的投资无疑是对美国不断升级的出口管制措施的直接回应，这些措施旨在削弱中国的半导体产业，尤其是拜登政府于2022年10月公布的一系列旨在阻止中国获取高端芯片及其生产设备的措施。

Despite Xi's repeated invocation of the dire need for greater economic security, aside from increasing R&D there were few effective measures the party could undertake in the short term. Although China stepped up efforts to reduce its reliance on the US dollar by denominating more trade in renminbi, its use of the dollar was unlikely to fall dramatically simply because there were no alternatives in the foreseeable future for China to settle trade and manage its huge foreign exchange reserves.69 Food self-sufficiency, another prized security goal Xi has emphasized repeatedly, is also unlikely to be achieved in the near term because China does not have enough arable land, and its food self-sufficiency ratio was only 66 percent as of 2020.70

尽管习近平反复强调迫切需要加强经济安全，但除了加大研发投入外，党在短期内能采取的有效措施寥寥无几。虽然中国加大了对美元的依赖，增加了人民币结算贸易，但美元使用量不太可能大幅下降，因为在可预见的未来，中国没有其他替代方案来结算贸易和管理其庞大的外汇储备。粮食自给自足是习近平反复强调的另一项重要的安全目标，但短期内也难以实现，因为中国耕地面积有限，截至2020年，粮食自给率仅为66%。

But Chinese leaders are unlikely to be deterred by the challenge of building up an economic fortress. The costs of such an undertaking will be staggering. "Forced import substitution" in the case of advance technologies will make China reallocate resources to economic activities for which it lacks a comparative advantage. Achieving food self-sufficiency by producing more grains domestically at the expense of higher-value cash crops will reduce income from agriculture. Shifting supplies away from the United States and its allies will cut competition and increase costs. Chinese manufacturers that rely excessively on the domestic market will not be competitive with their global peers. Regardless of the culpability of the US-China decoupling and tech war, the end result of China's response—a security-focused development strategy—will be less economic efficiency and lower growth for the long term. For the party and Xi, this seems a price worth paying if the alternative will place China at the mercy of a hostile West that sees a powerful China as an existential threat.

但中国领导人不太可能被构建经济堡垒的挑战吓倒。这项工程的代价将是巨大的。“强制进口替代”（尤其是在先进技术领域）将迫使中国把资源重新分配到自身缺乏比较优势的经济活动上。为了实现粮食自给自足，牺牲高价值经济作物的种植，增加国内粮食产量，将会降低农业收入。减少对美国及其盟友的依赖，会削弱竞争，增加成本。过度依赖国内市场的中国制造商将无法与全球同行竞争。无论中美脱钩和科技战的责任归属如何，中国最终采取的应对措施——以安全为中心的经济发展战略——都将导致长期经济效率降低和增长放缓。对于中共及习近平而言，如果另一种选择是让中国受制于将强大的中国视为生存威胁的敌对西方，那么这样的代价似乎是值得的。





Reversion to Statism





回归国家主义


The CCP's schizophrenic attitude toward the private sector is well-known. On the one hand, the party's imperative of sustaining performance legitimacy dictates a pragmatic approach to the private sector, the largest contributor to economic output. On the other hand, political distrust of private entrepreneurs, lingering ideological hostility to capitalism, and entrenched regime interests to preserve a large state sector motivate the party to discriminate against the private sector regardless of the loss of efficiency.71 In practice, such discrimination manifests itself in regulatory barriers restricting the entry of private firms into strategic sectors (such as finance, energy, and telecom), favorable access to credit and subsidies for SOEs, and harassment and mistreatment of private firms by local authorities that see them as easy prey.72 In spite of government discrimination, however, private firms thrived in the post-Tiananmen era, as evidenced by their growing share of GDP, urban employment, and exports.73

中共对私营部门的矛盾态度众所周知。一方面，为了维护执政的合法性，中共必须对私营部门采取务实的态度，因为私营部门是经济产出的最大贡献者。另一方面，对私营企业家的政治不信任、对资本主义挥之不去的意识形态敌意，以及根深蒂固的政权维护庞大国有部门的利益，促使执政党不顾效率损失，对私营部门进行歧视。71 在实践中，这种歧视表现为：监管壁垒限制私营企业进入战略部门（如金融、能源和电信），国有企业享有信贷和补贴的优惠待遇，以及地方政府将私营企业视为易受攻击的目标，对其进行骚扰和虐待。72 然而，尽管存在政府歧视，私营企业在后天安门时代依然蓬勃发展，其在GDP、城镇就业和出口中所占份额的增长便是明证。73

Complaints that "the state advances and the private retreats" (guojin min-tui) became more frequent toward the end of the Hu Jintao era, prompted mostly by the government's massive stimulus package implemented in 2009 to sustain growth following the global financial crisis. As the state sector was the primary beneficiary of the package, which consisted of four trillion yuan in fiscal spending and an infusion of bank credit several times that amount, the government's response elicited concerns that party policy toward the private sector was being reversed. Additionally, the government encouraged giant SOEs to acquire other (usually struggling) SOEs and even well-established private firms.74

在胡锦涛时代末期，“国进民退”的抱怨日益频繁，这主要是由于政府在2009年为应对全球金融危机而实施的大规模经济刺激计划所致。由于国有企业是该计划的主要受益者（该计划包括4万亿元人民币的财政支出和数倍于此的银行信贷注入），政府的应对措施引发了人们对党对私营部门政策逆转的担忧。此外，政府还鼓励大型国有企业收购其他（通常是经营困难的）国有企业，甚至收购成熟的民营企业。

In the post-Tiananmen era, the state had always maintained an extensive presence in the economy, but the pivot back to statism at the expense of the private sector became more pronounced after 2009.75 However, like the shift toward a more assertive foreign policy and a regressive domestic agenda, guojin mintui on the eve of Xi's rise to power lacked an ideologically coherent program and was notable for the absence of a high-profile crackdown on iconic private firms or well-known private entrepreneurs. All this would change under Xi.

在后天安门时代，国家一直对经济保持着广泛的影响力，但2009年后，以牺牲私营部门为代价的回归国家主义的趋势愈发明显。然而，与外交政策趋于强硬、国内政策趋于保守一样，习近平上台前夕的国民经济缺乏意识形态上的连贯性纲领，尤其值得注意的是，当时并未对标志性的私营企业或知名企业家进行大规模打压。这一切在习近平的领导下都将发生改变。

Before his ascent to the top, Xi had said or done few things that revealed his views of the private sector. His three-and-one-half-year stint as party chief of Zhejiang province (November 2002 to March 2007) may bolster his image as a probusiness official, but his record in Zhejiang contains no evidence of major initiatives that supported the private sector. As an astute politician, Xi was careful to avoid close ties with wealthy private entrepreneurs. Although his extended family members had reportedly amassed large fortunes through questionable business deals, Xi and his immediate family are not known to have been implicated in corruption.76

在登上权力巅峰之前，习近平很少公开表达或展现其对私营部门的看法。他担任浙江省委书记三年半（2002年11月至2007年3月）的经历或许强化了他亲商官员的形象，但他在浙江的政绩中并无任何支持私营部门的重大举措。作为一位精明的政治家，习近平谨慎地避免与富有的私营企业家建立密切联系。尽管据报道他的一些远亲通过可疑的商业交易积累了巨额财富，但习近平及其直系亲属并未卷入任何腐败丑闻。

Only after he became party chief did Xi reveal what he really thought about the relationship between the state and the private sector. His rhetoric grew more unabashedly supportive of the state sector after he quietly abandoned the reform blueprint unveiled with great fanfare in November 2013. In October 2016 he emphasized that SOEs are "an important material and political basis for socialism with Chinese characteristics and an important pillar and reliable force for the CCP's governance of the country," and that the party will "firmly and unwaveringly make SOEs stronger, bigger, and better."77

习近平担任中共中央总书记后，才真正揭示了他对国家与私营部门关系的看法。在悄然放弃了2013年11月高调公布的改革方案后，他对国有企业的支持言论变得更加公开。2016年10月，他强调国有企业是“中国特色社会主义的重要物质和政治基础，是中共治国的重要支柱和可靠力量”，并表示党将“坚定不移地把国有企业建设得更强大、更大、更好”。

In terms of policy, however, the party did not adopt one single major policy package to roll back the private sector. Early on, Xi launched a campaign to force private and foreign-invested companies to establish party organizations as a means of asserting political control.78 Later, policies that favored the state sector over the private sector were rolled out in a piecemeal fashion until Xi ordered a more drastic crackdown on the private sector that began in late 2020. The first prong of Xi's economic strategy to preserve the state sector as the "dominant entity" was the 2015 unveiling of "Made in China 2025." Although China had proposed similar industrial policy packages with aspirational goals in the past, "Made in China 2025," a ten-year, state-led industrial strategy to establish China's global dominance in the high-tech manufacturing industry and to reduce its dependence on foreign technology, was far more ambitious and controversial.79 China's main trading partners in the West saw it as an undisguised effort by China to displace the West as the global technological leader. The plan stipulated that China would attain 70 percent self-sufficiency in high-tech industries by 2025 and would achieve a leading position in global markets by 2049, the centennial of the People's Republic of China.80 In addition to the worrisome security implications, "Made in China 2025" also involved massive government subsidies and protectionist measures that were bound to conflict with the West's economic interests. At home, it would funnel huge resources to the state sector, which was tasked with realizing the ambitious goals.

然而，在政策层面，中共并未采取单一的重大政策方案来限制私营企业。习近平早期发起了一场运动，强制私营企业和外商投资企业建立党组织，以此来加强政治控制。之后，有利于国有企业而非私营企业的政策陆续出台，直到2020年底，习近平下令对私营企业进行更为严厉的打压。习近平旨在维护国有企业“主导地位”的经济战略的第一步，便是2015年提出的“中国制造2025”。尽管中国过去也曾提出过类似的产业政策方案，并设定了宏伟的目标，但“中国制造2025”——一项为期十年、由国家主导的产业战略，旨在确立中国在全球高科技制造业的主导地位，并降低对外国技术的依赖——则更具雄心，也更具争议性。中国在西方的主要贸易伙伴将其视为中国试图取代西方成为全球技术领导者的明目张胆之举。该计划规定，到2025年，中国高科技产业的自给率将达到70%，到2049年，即中华人民共和国成立一百周年之际，将在全球市场占据领先地位。除了令人担忧的安全隐患外，“中国制造2025”还涉及巨额政府补贴和保护主义措施，这些措施势必会与西方的经济利益产生冲突。在国内，它将向国有部门输送大量资源，由国有部门负责实现这些雄心勃勃的目标。

Another step the party undertook to bolster SOEs was to make them even bigger, a trend that had started under Hu. Giant SOEs directly under the control of the central government acquired small and poor-performing ones, ostensibly to increase the economies of scale. During Xi's first term, SASAC engineered some of the largest mergers of SOEs in history, such as the combination of CSR Corporation and CNR Corporation, two manufacturers of locomotives and rolling stock in 2015, as well as several others. Based on data provided by SASAC, such mergers did make the centrally controlled SOEs bigger, as measured by their assets. But their efficiency actually declined, and their debt-to-asset ratio rose.81

为加强国有企业实力，中共采取的另一项措施是扩大其规模，这一趋势始于胡锦涛时期。中央直接控制的巨型国有企业收购了规模小、业绩差的企业，表面上是为了提高规模经济效益。在习近平第一任期内，国资委主导了一些历史上规模最大的国有企业并购案，例如2015年中车集团和中车集团这两家机车车辆制造商的合并，以及其他几起并购案。根据国资委提供的数据，这些并购确实扩大了中央控制的国有企业的规模（以资产衡量）。但它们的效率实际上下降了，资产负债率上升了。

The government's direct intervention in the stock market in 2015 is another example of the revival of statism under Xi. Starting in June 2014, China's stock markets began a bull run. Investor exuberance, fueled in part by the official media, drove the main index on the Shanghai Stock Exchange up more than 150 percent within the year. When the bubble began to burst in mid-June 2015, the top leadership viewed the slide in stock prices as a negative reflection of its economic stewardship and ordered that the "national team"—mainly state-owned financial entities—pour trillions of yuan into the market to support the prices. This intervention failed miserably. In addition to the waste of huge amounts of money, the government-orchestrated rescue did not stop the crash. By the time the market stabilized in March 2016, the Shanghai index was down 45 percent from its peak.82 Although this was not the first time the Chinese state had intervened to prevent stock prices from collapsing, it had never before engineered such a broad, costly, and ultimately doomed effort.

2015年政府直接干预股市是习近平领导下国家主义复兴的又一例证。2014年6月起，中国股市开启牛市。在官方媒体的推波助澜下，投资者热情高涨，推动上海证券交易所主要股指在一年内上涨超过150%。2015年6月中旬，泡沫开始破裂，最高领导层将股价下跌视为其经济管理不善的体现，并下令由国有金融机构组成的“国家队”向市场注入数万亿元人民币以支撑股价。然而，这次干预彻底失败。政府主导的救助不仅浪费了巨额资金，也未能阻止股市崩盘。到 2016 年 3 月市场企稳时，上证指数已从峰值下跌了 45%。尽管这并非中国政府第一次干预股市以防止股价暴跌，但此前从未进行过如此大规模、代价高昂且最终失败的干预行动。

In addition to channeling resources to the state sector, the government also implemented policies that systematically hurt the private sector. An early indication of policies that were less friendly to private entrepreneurs was the dramatic reduction in loans to the private sector by state-owned banks. In 2013 about 57 percent of all loans flowed to nonfinancial private firms. But this trend was reversed in 2014, when only 34 percent of such loans went to nonfinancial private firms. By 2015, only a trickle of credit—19 percent—was made available to nonfinancial firms. When the government launched its "deleveraging" campaign in 2016, private firms were hit especially hard. In that year, their share of credit collapsed to 11 percent.83

除了将资源导向国有部门外，政府还实施了一系列系统性地损害私营部门的政策。国有银行大幅削减对私营部门的贷款，便是这些政策对私营企业家不太友好的早期迹象。2013年，约57%的贷款流向了非金融私营企业。但这一趋势在2014年发生了逆转，当年只有34%的此类贷款流向了非金融私营企业。到2015年，流向非金融企业的信贷仅占19%。2016年，政府启动“去杠杆化”运动，私营企业受到的冲击尤为严重。当年，它们的信贷份额骤降至11%。

Private firms were easy targets during the deleveraging campaign between 2016 and mid-2018 because, in spite of their efficiency, they had costly and unstable access to credit. As state-owned banks require collateral from private firms and fear responsibility if their loans to private firms go sour, private firms must primarily rely on the shadow banking system (trust companies and wealth management firms) to borrow short-term loans at higher interest rates. Consequently, when the government required that the entire financial system reduce its leverage, the supply of credit to private firms fell because the state-owned banks could call back loans to shrink their balance sheets, whereas the shadow banking system, which indirectly also relied on the formal banking system for funding, was forced to cut credit to private firms.84

在2016年至2018年中期的去杠杆化运动中，私营企业很容易成为目标，因为尽管它们效率高，但获得信贷的成本高昂且不稳定。由于国有银行要求私营企业提供抵押品，并且担心如果其对私营企业的贷款出现不良后果，私营企业不得不主要依赖影子银行体系（信托公司和财富管理公司）以更高的利率借入短期贷款。因此，当政府要求整个金融体系降低杠杆率时，私营企业的信贷供应下降，因为国有银行可以收回贷款以缩减资产负债表，而间接依赖正规银行体系融资的影子银行体系则被迫削减对私营企业的信贷。

The negative impact of deleveraging on the private sector can be seen in the slower growth of the number of private firms and their employment, and, more important, the relative decline of the private sector as an investor in the domestic economy. In the three years (2013-2015) prior to the deleveraging campaign, the number of private firms and their employment numbers had grown, on average, 20.6 percent and 11.9 percent, respectively. During the three years of deleveraging (2016-2018), the corresponding numbers were 18.1 percent and 10.1 percent, respectively, indicating the slower growth of the private sector.85

去杠杆化对私营部门的负面影响体现在私营企业数量及其就业人数增长放缓，更重要的是，私营部门作为国内经济投资者的作用相对下降。在去杠杆化行动之前的三年（2013-2015年），私营企业数量及其就业人数平均分别增长了20.6%和11.9%。而在去杠杆化的三年（2016-2018年）期间，这两个数字分别下降至18.1%和10.1%，表明私营部门的增长速度放缓。

Investment data during this period paint an even clearer picture of the retreat of the private sector under Xi. In 2016 and 2017, the height of the deleveraging campaign, private sector investment in fixed assets grew only 2.8 and 5.2 percent, respectively.
